item.title: EEUU planea revocar visas de turismo y negocios de hasta 200.000 extranjeros: AP
item.description: El Gobierno de Donald Trump se está preparando para revocar los visados de negocios y turismo de hasta 200.000 extranjeros que han solicitado o están solicitando actualmente el estatuto de asilo en Estados Unidos, informó el lunes la agencia Associated Press.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno de Donald Trump se está preparando para revocar los visados de negocios y turismo de hasta 200.000 extranjeros que han solicitado o están solicitando actualmente el estatuto de asilo en Estados Unidos, informó el lunes la agencia Associated Press. El reporte citaba documentos del Departamento de Estado obtenidos por la AP y a dos funcionarios estadounidenses. Si esta medida se llevara a cabo, sería la mayor revocación masiva de visados de la historia de Estados Unidos, según la AP. Más temprano el lunes, el subsecretario de Estado, Christopher Landau, dijo en X que el sistema de inmigración estadounidense "lleva mucho tiempo desbordado por solicitudes de asilo infundadas". El Departamento de Estado no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Trump ha llevado a cabo una agresiva campaña de represión en materia de inmigración que, según él, tiene como objetivo mejorar la seguridad nacional. Las organizaciones de derechos humanos afirman que esta campaña ha violado los derechos a la libertad de expresión y al debido proceso, y ha creado un entorno inseguro, especialmente para las minorías étnicas, que han expresado su preocupación por la discriminación racial.

item.title: Nevada sues to block Trump administration's Colorado River plan
item.description: Nevada sued the Trump administration on Monday to block its plans for slashing water supplies from the drought-stricken Colorado River, saying it could devastate the state and would violate the laws governing the river.
item.dc:creator: Tom Hals
item.content:encoded: Nevada sued the Trump administration on Monday to block its plans for slashing water supplies from the drought-stricken Colorado River, saying it could devastate the state and would violate the laws governing the river. The Department of the Interior on Friday [USN:L1N44I0LY TEXT:"finalized its plan"] that included a 21% reduction in water from the river to California, Nevada and Arizona for two years starting in 2027. The cuts to the three so-called lower basin states could nearly double after 2028, a move that Arizona and Nevada have said would have huge consequences for their economies. The four so-called upper basin states — Colorado, Utah, New Mexico and Wyoming — face no mandatory cuts under the new 10-year plan to manage the river that provides water to one in 10 Americans and generates power for 6 million people. The plan is up for review every two years and the states were unable to agree on how to share the water after more than three years of talks to replace a plan that expires this year. Upper basin states refused to take mandatory cuts to their water supply from the river, arguing they already face steep reductions due to the decades-long drought in the western United States. The three lower basin states say all seven states that share the river must make cutbacks in water use. The lawsuit by Nevada, the Colorado River Commission of Nevada and the Southern Nevada Water Authority is the first to challenge the plan. It was filed in federal court in Las Vegas and named as defendants the Department of the Interior, Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation and its commissioner, Aubrey Bettencourt. The Interior Department declined to comment and the Bureau of Reclamation did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lawsuit alleged the administration violated administrative law, environmental law and the group of treaties, agreements and court rulings known as the Law of the River. It said the administration did not comply with requirements to consider reasonable alternatives and foreseeable economic impacts, to fully respond to comments or to adequately analyze mitigation measures. "Consequently, decisionmakers and stakeholders are left to guess at how federal defendants interpret and apply the Law of the River, which all agree governs the proposed action," the lawsuit said.

item.title: Power supply firm Aggreko files for US IPO
item.description: Power supply firm Aggreko has filed for a U.S. initial public offering, the firm said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Power supply firm Aggreko has filed for a U.S. initial public offering, the firm said on Monday. The company intends to list its ordinary shares on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "AGKO", but it did not disclose the number of shares to be offered or the proposed price range. Aggreko's public filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission underscores a broader rush by power companies to tap U.S. equity markets as investors bet on rising electricity demand and the need for new energy infrastructure. Nuclear companies X-Energy (XE.O) and Standard Nuclear (STDN.N) went public through traditional IPOs this year. Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and BofA Securities are serving as joint lead bookrunning managers for Aggreko's offering, while Barclays and Morgan Stanley will be bookrunning managers.

item.title: Former NBA players not eligible for WNBA, sources say
item.description: Two former NBA players who sought to enter the 2027 WNBA draft are not eligible to participate in the women's basketball league, according to sources around the league on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: Two former NBA players who sought to enter the 2027 WNBA draft are not eligible to participate in the women's basketball league, according to sources around the league on Monday. Enes Kanter Freedom, who played in the National Basketball Association for over a decade from 2011, and Royce White, who spent one season in the NBA, had each announced their intention to play in the league, claiming to be transgender women. The sources described the move as an effort to sow division within the WNBA and court attention, amid a nationwide firestorm over U.S. President Donald Trump's [USN:L1N4310YB TEXT:"repeated efforts"] to ban transgender women from women's sports. Reuters was not immediately able to reach Kanter Freedom or White for comment. There are no active, openly transgender players in the WNBA, which does not currently have a specific, publicly available policy on transgender participation. The league is in ongoing conversations with stakeholders on the issue. Comments made by Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham in an ESPN interview last month lit the fuse for controversy, with the former second-round pick telling the broadcaster: "I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men." The remarks prompted outcry from some longstanding fans of the league, who skew more politically liberal, while others rallied to Cunningham's side, with demonstrations in her support popping up outside Fever games. The players' union, the WNBPA, released a statement this month declaring they would not be used as "political pawns". "Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm," they said. Kanter Freedom said on social media on Sunday that he was ejected from a game between Chicago Sky and the Fever after getting into a verbal spat with 2022 assists leader Natasha Cloud.

item.title: Manchester City cierra acuerdo con Palmeiras por atacante Allan
item.description: El Manchester City ha llegado a un acuerdo por una cifra de hasta 34,2 millones de libras (46,61 millones de dólares) para fichar al extremo del Palmeiras Allan Elias, informaron el lunes medios británicos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Manchester City ha llegado a un acuerdo por una cifra de hasta 34,2 millones de libras (46,61 millones de dólares) para fichar al extremo del Palmeiras Allan Elias, informaron el lunes medios británicos. Según reportes de la BBC y Sky Sports, el City pagará inicialmente 32 millones de libras por el brasileño de 22 años, con 2 millones de libras adicionales en posibles complementos. Allan, que también juega como centrocampista ofensivo, se incorporó a la cantera del Palmeiras en 2019 y debutó con el primer equipo en enero de 2025. Desde entonces, ha disputado 96 partidos con el club, en los que ha marcado nueve goles y ha dado 12 asistencias, y formó parte del equipo que ganó el Campeonato Paulista en 2024 y 2026. Según la prensa brasileña, se espera que se pierda el partido de cuartos de final de la Copa de Brasil del miércoles contra el Santos, mientras se prepara para el traspaso. Allan sustituirá a su compatriota Savinho, quien, de acuerdo con reportes, está a punto de fichar por el Tottenham Hotspur procedente del City. (1 dólar = 0,7337 libras)

item.title: Marlins activate 1B/OF Kyle Stowers (hamstring) from 10-day IL
item.description: Ahead of their three-game interleague series opener against the Boston Red Sox on Monday, the Miami Marlins activated first baseman/outfielder Kyle Stowers from the 10-day injured list.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ahead of their three-game interleague series opener against the Boston Red Sox on Monday, the Miami Marlins activated first baseman/outfielder Kyle Stowers from the 10-day injured list. Stowers, 28, a first-time All-Star last season, was placed on the IL with a Grade 1 left hamstring strain on Aug. 11, retroactive to Aug. 10. Stowers, who entered Monday batting .242 this season with 16 homers and 52 RBIs in 94 games, started at first base and batted third. "I feel good ... I feel more comfortable this time than I did last time," Stowers said, referring to his IL stint in April for a right hamstring strain that delayed his season debut until April 19. "Mentally, this was my best (IL stint) this time. The last couple times, it was really hard mentally on me. This time I was really bummed, but I made it what it was. It was an injury, didn't make it any deeper than it needed to be. I was a lot more clear-headed this time with the injury. Just took it day by day. I think that was the biggest growth I've made so far." Selected by the Baltimore Orioles in the second round of the 2019 draft, Stowers played parts of three seasons with the Orioles (2022-24) before being dealt to the Marlins. He has hit .249 with 47 homers and 160 RBIs in 328 games. In a corresponding move, the Marlins optioned third baseman Deyvison De Los Santos to Triple-A Jacksonville. The 23-year-old made his major league debut March 29 and is 3-for-9 with a double. The Marlins entered play Monday four games behind the San Diego Padres for the final National League wild-card spot. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jueza EEUU desestima recurso contra la ampliación de las perforaciones en alta mar de Trump
item.description: Una jueza federal de Alaska desestimó el lunes una demanda presentada por grupos ecologistas que impugnaban la decisión del presidente Donald Trump de permitir la perforación en alta mar a lo largo de amplias franjas del litoral que anteriormente estaban protegidas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Una jueza federal de Alaska desestimó el lunes una demanda presentada por grupos ecologistas que impugnaban la decisión del presidente Donald Trump de permitir la perforación en alta mar a lo largo de amplias franjas del litoral que anteriormente estaban protegidas. La jueza federal de distrito Sharon L. Gleason consideró que la demanda presentada por varios grupos, entre ellos el Northern Alaska Environmental Center, era prematura, ya que la perforación no era inminente en las aguas federales que los predecesores de Trump habían declarado zonas prohibidas. Gleason no se pronunció sobre si los presidentes tienen autoridad legal para revocar la exclusión de zonas costeras de la perforación decidida por sus predecesores y dejó la puerta abierta para que las organizaciones vuelvan a presentar su demanda. Earthjustice, una organización de defensa cuyos abogados interpusieron la demanda, afirmó en un comunicado que la organización sigue considerando que las medidas de Trump fueron ilegales y que volvería a presentar el caso si las autoridades federales ampliaran las perforaciones en alta mar. "Este Gobierno ha estado haciendo todo lo que está en su mano para abrir nuestras costas a la explotación de combustibles fósiles. Seguimos manteniendo que el intento del presidente Trump de abrir las zonas retiradas a la concesión de licencias petroleras es ilegal, y tenemos la intención de seguir adelante con esas reclamaciones si las actividades en alta mar se vislumbran en el horizonte", dijo la organización en un comunicado. El Departamento de Justicia no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. El expresidente demócrata Joe Biden prohibió nuevas explotaciones de petróleo y gas en alta mar a lo largo de la mayor parte de las costas estadounidenses antes de que Trump asumiera el cargo, aunque la medida se consideró en gran medida simbólica, ya que no afectaba a las zonas donde ya se estaban realizando perforaciones y abarcaba principalmente áreas sin importantes perspectivas de desarrollo. Trump trató de revocar esa medida como parte de una serie de decretos emitidos a las pocas horas de su posesión, destinados a impulsar la producción de petróleo y gas del país —que ya se encontraba en niveles récord— y a desmantelar los esfuerzos de Biden para hacer frente al cambio climático.

item.title: Reports: Texans obtain WR Kayshon Boutte from Patriots
item.description: The Houston Texans are acquiring receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots for safety Jaylen Reed and a seventh-round draft pick in 2028, according to multiple reports Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Houston Texans are acquiring receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots for safety Jaylen Reed and a seventh-round draft pick in 2028, according to multiple reports Monday. Boutte fills a need after Houston lost second-year pro Jayden Higgins for the season due to a torn ACL sustained on Aug. 18. Boutte, 24, caught 33 passes for 551 yards and a career-high six touchdowns in 14 games (10 starts) last season. In 2024, he established career bests of 43 catches and 589 yards. Overall, Boutte has 78 receptions for 1,159 yards and nine touchdowns in 34 NFL games (23 starts). Reed, 23, played in seven games (one start) as a rookie last season and had 14 tackles and one fumble recovery. He was a sixth-round pick in the 2025 draft. --Field Level Media

item.title: Campaña de Lula se plantea restringir contratación de trabajadores autónomos en posible nuevo mandato
item.description: El Gobierno brasileño está evaluando mecanismos para frenar el recurso a trabajadores contratados como personas jurídicas en lugar de como empleados, de cara a una posible reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, dijo el lunes el ministro de Hacienda, Dario Durigan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno brasileño está evaluando mecanismos para frenar el recurso a trabajadores contratados como personas jurídicas en lugar de como empleados, de cara a una posible reelección del presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, dijo el lunes el ministro de Hacienda, Dario Durigan. El plan podría reducir al mínimo el déficit de las pensiones en Brasil y proporcionar una mayor protección en materia de seguridad social a los trabajadores, explicó Durigan a Broadcast, el servicio de noticias del periódico local Estadão. "A una empresa en la que el 80% de su plantilla esté contratada como autónomos, se le podría exigir, en su momento, que realice cotizaciones a la seguridad social", afirmó. Los trabajadores contratados como personas jurídicas suelen percibir un salario bruto más elevado, mientras que las empresas se benefician normalmente de unos costos laborales más bajos, ya que no están obligadas a pagar impuestos sobre las nóminas, cotizaciones al fondo de indemnización por despido ni otras prestaciones. Broadcast presentó a Durigan como representante de la campaña presidencial de Lula, quien se presentará a la reelección en las próximas elecciones de octubre. Durigan también abogó por una revisión de los impuestos corporativos citando los debates sobre los impuestos a las nóminas y los intereses sobre el capital, un tipo de remuneración para los accionistas.

item.title: Chelsea start Alonso era with exciting 3-2 win at Fulham
item.description: Chelsea began life under new coach Xabi Alonso with a breathless 3-2 win at West London neighbours Fulham in the Premier League on Monday as their exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer all found the net.
item.dc:creator: William Schomberg
item.content:encoded: Chelsea began life under new coach Xabi Alonso with a breathless 3-2 win at West London neighbours Fulham in the Premier League on Monday as their exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer all found the net. Chelsea got off to a dream start after 31 seconds when Palmer – looking back to his best after struggling with an injury last season – passed to Joao Pedro and the Brazilian flicked the ball over goalkeeper Bernd Leno. Fulham equalised when Josh King beat Chelsea goalkeeper Robert Sanchez at his near post in the 24th minute. But two of Chelsea's new signings then combined in the 41st as central defender Maxence Lacroix jinked down the right before cutting the ball back to the club's £117 million ($159.47 million) [USN:L1N43N13K TEXT:"record signing Rogers"], who made no mistake. Four minutes into the second half, Palmer slotted the ball through Leno’s legs after he was fed by Joao Pedro. Fulham's Gonzalo Garcia, on his league debut after signing from Real Madrid, gave the hosts hope by heading in after Sanchez could only parry a Timothy Castagne shot in the 54th. Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez – a lynchpin of World Cup runners-up Argentina who has been linked with a move to Manchester City - was greeted with loud boos from the home fans when he came on as a substitute midway through the second half. Fulham then had a great chance to level again through Antonee Robinson in the 78th minute but his chip over a stranded Sanchez went wide and Chelsea held out to claim the points. ($1 = 0.7337 pounds)

item.title: Milho atinge maior cotação em 3 anos em Chicago por menor produção nos EUA
item.description: Os contratos futuros do milho dispararam na bolsa de Chicago para máximas de três anos nesta segunda-feira, depois que uma expedição técnica à região produtora de milho e soja dos EUA na semana passada revelou que a safra do cereal do país estava em condições piores do que muitos esperavam.
item.dc:creator: Heather Schlitz
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros do milho dispararam na bolsa de Chicago para máximas de três anos nesta segunda-feira, depois que uma expedição técnica à região produtora de milho e soja dos EUA na semana passada revelou que a safra do cereal do país estava em condições piores do que muitos esperavam. O trigo atingiu seu maior nível em cerca de dois anos, à medida que as retaliações mútuas entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia restringiram as exportações dos portos do Mar Negro, embora os futuros tenham reduzido os ganhos no final do pregão. A soja caiu, pressionada pela queda do petróleo, mas as perdas foram limitadas pela forte demanda de exportação pela soja norte-americana. O contrato de milho mais negociado fechou com alta de 7 centavos, a US$5,155, após atingir US$5,2525 por bushel, a maior cotação desde 2023. A maioria dos contratos de milho registrou máximas históricas. "O mercado noturno disparou com a divulgação na sexta-feira, que saiu após o fechamento do pregão", disse Joe Davis, diretor de vendas de commodities da Futures International. A consultoria Pro Farmer estimou na sexta-feira que a produção de milho dos EUA em 2026 ficará bem abaixo das previsões do governo, após uma visita a sete dos principais Estados produtores ter constatado safras abaixo do esperado, prejudicadas pelo clima adverso do verão. A Pro Farmer projetou que os agricultores colheriam uma safra de milho de 15,344 bilhões de bushels, uma queda de 9,9% em relação a 2025, mas ainda assim a terceira maior já registrada, com um rendimento médio de 173,2 bushels por acre. A estimativa da Pro Farmer para os EUA, se concretizada, seria a mais baixa desde 2020. "As pessoas ficaram chocadas ao ver esse número", disse Davis. Os operadores também estão cautelosos quanto à possibilidade de que o fenômeno climático El Niño reduza a produção de milho no Brasil e estão apreensivos quanto à capacidade de exportação da Ucrânia, segundo analistas. O trigo fechou com alta de 0,25 centavo, a US$6,995 o bushel, reduzindo os ganhos após atingir a maior cotação em cerca de dois anos. A soja encerrou com queda de 15,25 centavos, a US$12,2425 o bushel.

item.title: TRADING DAY Tech, tariffs & Treasuries
item.description: U.S. bond yields fell and tech weighed on U.S. stocks on Monday, as investors digested a raft of economic measures and developments coming out of Washington: U.S. Treasury's plans to increase buybacks of long-dated bonds, new 'economic D-Day' sanctions to isolate Iran, and the threat of new tariffs on Canada.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: U.S. bond yields fell and tech weighed on [USN:L4N44L0KA TEXT:"U.S. stocks"] on Monday, as investors digested a raft of economic measures and developments coming out of Washington: U.S. Treasury's plans to increase [USN:L1N44H0RB TEXT:"buybacks"] of long-dated bonds, new [USN:L1N44L0ES TEXT:"'economic D-Day'"] sanctions to isolate Iran, and the threat of new tariffs on [USN:L8N44L114 TEXT:"Canada"]. In my column today, I look at whether U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent faces a [USN:L6N44K07X TEXT:"credibility problem"]. The evidence is mounting — the Treasury's recent surprise FX and bond market interventions have unnerved investors, and by Bessent's own stated goals of reducing the deficit and lowering bond yields, he is falling short. If you have more time to read, here are a few articles I recommend to help you make sense of what happened in markets today. [USN:S8N40O00O TEXT:"US unveils 'economic D-Day' of sanctions to isolate Iran"] [USN:L8N44L114 TEXT:"Trump threatens 50% tariffs on all cars and trucks from Canada amid trade fight"] [USN:L6N44H0PG TEXT:"Bond market anxiety raises stakes for Warsh's debut Jackson Hole speech"] [USN:L6N44I0M9 TEXT:"Traders are bracing for an increasingly hawkish ECB"] [USN:P8N43T02S TEXT:"Alibaba shares slide after $10.2 billion AI share sale offered at sharp discount"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Asia in the red (KOSPI -3%, Nikkei -0.7%), [USN:L6N44L0CP TEXT:"Europe"] flat, UK +0.4%, Wall Street mixed (Dow +0.3%, S&P 500 -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.8%) SECTORS/SHARES: Eight sectors on the S&P 500 rise, three fall. Comms services, financials, utilities, consumer staples up 1% or more, tech -1.6%. Nvidia -3%; Seagate, SanDisk, Micron all down ~6%. Expedia +5.5%, Visa +3%, Walmart +2.7%. FX: [USN:L1N44L018 TEXT:"Dollar"] +0.2%, its best day in two weeks. CAD is biggest G10 loser on new tariffs. Bitcoin extends rally, +2% to nudge $80k. Bitcoin +25% in just over a week. BONDS: U.S. yields down 5 bps at long end, curve flattens. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N44K03U TEXT:"Oil"] -2.5%, only its second fall in 14 sessions. [USN:L4N44L00O TEXT:"Gold"] +1% to highest since mid-May. Today's Talking Points: Vigilance against the vigilantes U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent seems to be stepping up the fight against the "bond vigilantes". CNBC reported on Monday that part of his arsenal could be cash at the Treasury General Account to fund the purchase of longer-dated bonds instead of issuing short-term bills. Markets seemed to give the idea the thumbs up, with the 30-year yield falling 5 basis points and the curve flattening. But is the TGA really a longer-term source of funding for what Bessent last week called a "Treasury Twist"? Apart from emergencies, Treasury wants a chunky TGA balance. Bill issuance is rising, and so too is Treasury's reliance on bills for funding. This increases rollover risk, which necessitates a larger TGA buffer. Leaning more heavily on short-term bill issuance and simultaneously reducing cash on hand to mitigate rollover risk would seem to be a counter-intuitive and dicey proposition. Tariff tremors Talking of firepower, U.S. President Donald Trump has loaded up the tariff guns again, and is turning them on an ally, neighbor, and key trading partner Canada. Trump is threatening to impose 50% levies on certain Canadian goods, including all cars, trucks and auto parts. These duties will kick in on January 1 next year if no agreement is reached by then. Canada is not flinching. Not yet, anyway. Prime Minister Mark Carney has retaliated with "dollar for dollar" tariffs on imports of U.S. steel, electronics and other products, to take effect on September 8. Trump's approval ratings are at an all-time low, and with the midterms looming, perhaps he feels the need to flex some muscle on the international stage. For his part, perhaps Carney senses Trump's domestic vulnerability so is taking up the fight. Either way, relations between the two countries are deteriorating. Ace in the Jackson Hole Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will deliver the keynote address at the Kansas City Fed's annual Jackson Hole symposium on Friday. The eyes of the financial world are on him. Warsh wants to improve the Fed communications strategy, but only three months into his tenure, his communications have raised more questions than answers. How does he plan to get inflation back to target? How committed is he to the 2% inflation goal? Will he resist President Trump's demand for lower interest rates? His task has arguably been complicated by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who last week said Treasury will temporarily expand buybacks of long-dated bonds. Essentially, Treasury wants to get yields down, juice GDP, and grow the economy out of the debt hole it's in. But this is inflationary, and inflation has already been above target for more than five years. Warsh has said bond yields are a useful signal, and Bessent wants to actively massage them lower. Contradictions that require clearer communication. What could move markets tomorrow? item.title: Seoul says South Korea and US vow close cooperation on North Korea
item.description: South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke on Monday, and Seoul said they agreed to maintain close communication and cooperation on resolving the North Korean nuclear issue, South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported.
item.dc:creator: David Brunnstrom
item.content:encoded: South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke on Monday, and Seoul said they agreed to maintain close communication and cooperation on resolving the North Korean nuclear issue, South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported. The U.S. State Department issued only a brief statement on the phone call, which comes at a [USN:L4N44H048 TEXT:"period of tension between the allies"]. President Donald Trump recently announced a [USN:L1N44L0R2 TEXT:"scaling back of joint military exercises"] and [USN:L4N44H048 TEXT:"praised nuclear-armed North Korea"], while saying that Seoul had not helped his efforts to try to denuclearize Iran. The State Department said Rubio and Cho discussed "a range of issues in the U.S.-ROK Alliance," referring to South Korea by the initials of its official name, the Republic of Korea. "The Secretary noted the need for the two countries to remain in close coordination on matters that are integral to the Alliance," it added. Yonhap said that in a statement on their talks, South Korea's Foreign Ministry did not mention whether the diplomats reaffirmed their usual commitment to North Korea's denuclearization, despite their emphasis on the importance of cooperation on the North Korean nuclear issue. "The minister and secretary agreed to continue close communication and cooperation between South Korea and the U.S. for peace on the Korean Peninsula and the resolution of North Korea's nuclear issue while maintaining a solid combined defense posture," Yonhap quoted the ministry release as saying. It cited Cho as saying that Seoul would do its best to help ensure Trump's recent message for North Korea would lead to the resumption of dialogue between Washington and Pyongyang, and peace on the peninsula. TRUMP'S OUTREACH TESTS ALLIANCE Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un last week, coupled with his criticism of Seoul, has raised concern among analysts that Trump's unpredictability [USN:L1N44L07B TEXT:"could strain alliances that have long maintained peace in Asia"]. Cho said last week that Trump's order to curb the military drills appeared aimed in part at pressuring Seoul to support U.S. efforts in the Iran war, alongside other unresolved issues such as investment. He said one potential source of friction could be South Korea's pledge to invest $350 billion in the United States under a trade deal signed last year. Seoul has yet to announce details of the investment plan, although Cho said Washington had sent Seoul a proposal outlining projects that could be considered. Yonhap cited the ministry statement as saying that the two sides agreed to work toward "mutually beneficial" outcomes on various pending issues, including tariffs, investment and security cooperation. It said Cho underscored the Seoul government's commitment to making substantive contributions to help restore free passage through the Strait of Hormuz, while noting the active leadership of Trump and the U.S. in addressing the Middle East issue. It said Cho and Rubio agreed to meet in the near future to have in-depth discussions on key pending issues.

item.content:encoded: Manchester City have agreed a deal worth up to 34.2 million pounds ($46.61 million) to sign Palmeiras winger Allan Elias, British media reported on Monday. According to BBC and Sky Sports reports, City will pay an initial £32 million for the 22-year-old Brazilian, with a further £2 million in potential add-ons. Allan, who also plays as an attacking midfielder, joined Palmeiras' youth set up in 2019 and made his senior debut in January 2025. He has since played 96 times for the club, scoring nine goals with 12 assists, and was part of the side that won the Sao Paulo top-flight Campeonato Paulista in 2024 and 2026. He is expected to miss Wednesday's Copa do Brasil quarter-final against Santos as he prepares for the move, according to Brazilian media reports. Allan is set to replace fellow Brazilian Savinho, who is reportedly nearing a move from City to Tottenham Hotspur. ($1 = 0.7337 pounds)

item.title: US Supreme Court lifts a judicial hurdle to Trump's mail-in ballot curbs
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday lifted a judicial decision blocking President Donald Trump's administration from implementing his executive order to restrict the use of mail-in ballots ahead of the November midterm elections that will decide control of Congress - though another remains.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday lifted a judicial decision blocking President Donald Trump 's administration from implementing his executive order to restrict the use of mail-in ballots ahead of the November midterm elections that will decide control of Congress - though another remains. The justices granted a Justice Department emergency request to put on hold an injunction that Boston-based U.S. Judge Indira Talwani's imposed in June preventing the Republican president from proceeding with his directive in a coalition of 23 mostly Democratic-governed states and Washington, D.C. that had sued to stop it. The court has a 6-3 conservative majority. The three liberal justices dissented from the decision. The Supreme Court's action leaves open the door to the states suing again in the coming months as the midterm contest approaches. Trump's executive order, issued in March, directed the Department of Homeland Security to compile and transmit to the states a list of U.S. citizens eligible to vote in each state, and the Justice Department to prioritize investigating and prosecuting state and local election officials who issue ballots to people deemed "not eligible" to vote in federal elections. It also required the U.S. Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on each state's approved mail-in ballot list. The Postal Service recently moved to [USN:FWN4260WR TEXT:"implement"] Trump's directive. Trump has [USN:FWN3UA08Z TEXT:"vowed"] to end the use of mail-in ballots nationwide before the midterms, and has long cast doubt on the security of such ballots, although evidence of voter fraud is rare. Republicans are seeking to retain control of Congress in the hotly contested midterms. Restricting mail-in ballots would stand to disproportionately benefit Republicans given that Democratic voters traditionally have been more likely to use mail-in ballots than Republican voters. In June, Talwani ruled that the president lacked the authority to order changes in how states administer federal elections, noting that under the U.S. Constitution, states have the role of determining voter-eligibility requirements. The judge also noted that federal agencies lack the ability to compile accurate citizen lists for each state. The Justice Department had said the lawsuit challenging Trump's directive was premature and that the states did not have the required legal standing at this stage to sue. The agencies have not yet taken any concrete actions that impact the states and so any harm they allege is speculative, the administration said. The states contend that their claims are not hypothetical and that the administration's "rushed effort to change the rules of mail voting on the eve of the November midterms risks disenfranchising a substantial number of voters." The judge rejected the administration's arguments, finding that the suit was not filed too soon and that the states had legal standing because they would face election administration disruption, compliance costs and a credible threat of criminal prosecution. Trump's executive order is part of his wider efforts to make fundamental changes in U.S. elections. Trump, who has made false claims of widespread fraud in U.S. elections including his 2020 loss to Democrat Joe Biden, has pressed the Republican-controlled Congress to pass a contentious package of voting restrictions called the SAVE America Act.

item.title: CONSOLIDA EUA anunciam “Dia D econômico” de sanções para isolar Irã
item.description: Os EUA anunciaram nesta segunda-feira uma ampliação das sanções secundárias que, segundo esperam, “cortará todas as linhas de vida econômicas” que sustentam o Irã, enquanto o governo do presidente Donald Trump se esforça para resolver uma guerra impopular que tem pressionado para cima os preços da energia.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Humeyra Pamuk
item.content:encoded: Os EUA anunciaram nesta segunda-feira uma ampliação das sanções secundárias que, segundo esperam, “cortará todas as linhas de vida econômicas” que sustentam o Irã, enquanto o governo do presidente Donald Trump se esforça para resolver uma guerra impopular que tem pressionado para cima os preços da energia. O secretário do Tesouro, Scott Bessent, revelou o que descreveu como um “Dia D econômico”, que visa dar um aviso final aos países para que cortem seus laços comerciais com o Irã ou corram o risco de ter empresas e entidades importantes excluídas do sistema financeiro baseado no dólar. “Estamos lançando um ataque econômico contra as conexões financeiras do Irã em todo o mundo. Nosso objetivo é cortar todas as linhas de vida econômicas que sustentam esse regime tirânico até que Teerã fique isolada”, disse Bessent em uma coletiva de imprensa. No entanto, ele não quis identificar os países que seriam alvo das medidas ou informar quando essas sanções entrariam em vigor. A medida faz parte dos esforços dos EUA para pressionar o Irã a pôr fim aos ataques a navios no Golfo Pérsico e, mais recentemente, por meio de seus aliados, no Mar Vermelho, que Teerã lançou depois que os EUA e Israel iniciaram ataques aéreos contra o país em fevereiro. O Irã afirmou que isso terá o efeito oposto. O Irã passou décadas sob camadas de sanções norte-americanas e internacionais que abalaram sua economia, mas não dissuadiram sua liderança. Quase seis meses se passaram desde que os EUA e Israel lançaram ataques contra o Irã, desencadeando um conflito que paralisou o transporte marítimo na região, restringiu o fluxo de petróleo e causou prejuízos aos EUA e à economia global. Os preços do petróleo recuaram nesta segunda-feira, após duas semanas de alta, à medida que os investidores realizaram lucros antes do anúncio dos EUA. “NINGUÉM” ESTÁ FORA DO ALCANCE DAS SANÇÕES Bessent já havia solicitado a cooperação da China, o maior comprador de petróleo iraniano há vários anos, embora o bloqueio dos EUA aos portos do Irã, renovado em meados de julho, já tenha reduzido o fluxo de petróleo iraniano para a China. Especialistas afirmam que Washington teme uma retaliação chinesa a quaisquer sanções contra seus bancos antes das negociações previstas para o próximo mês entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, sendo que quaisquer restrições sobre exportações chinesas de minerais essenciais são especialmente delicadas. Questionado sobre os bancos chineses nesta segunda-feira, Bessent disse: “Queremos deixar claro aqui hoje que ninguém está acima do alcance das sanções dos EUA.” O Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China afirmou que sanções e táticas de pressão não ajudam e que Pequim faria o que fosse necessário para proteger os interesses da China. Bessent disse que o Departamento do Tesouro mapeou as redes, os facilitadores e os canais financeiros que o Irã usa para contrabandear petróleo e burlar as sanções. Ele afirmou que Washington trabalharia com seus parceiros para atingir qualquer fonte de “receita ilícita” do Irã. O departamento afirmou que o governo iraniano estava utilizando cinco setores — ativos digitais, tecnologia, ouro, aviação e transporte marítimo — para sustentar sua economia, e que esses setores estavam sob ameaça de sanções. O Tesouro também impôs sanções a quase 60 entidades, indivíduos e embarcações. Trump ameaçou aplicar tarifas sobre mercadorias provenientes de países que mantêm relações comerciais com o Irã, entre os quais Turquia, Iraque e Índia, embora a Suprema Corte tenha derrubado a base legal para tais tributações. O Irã rejeitou a ameaça dos Estados Unidos e emitiu um novo alerta à navegação, afirmando que embarcações não devem transitar pelo Estreito de Ormuz sem sua autorização, listando 45 navios que, segundo ele, violaram suas regras e ameaçando retaliação contra qualquer transferência de navio para navio envolvendo essas embarcações. NEGOCIAÇÕES COM O PAQUISTÃO, PROJÉTIL ATINGE PETROLEIRO O chefe do Exército do Paquistão, Asim Munir, que estabeleceu um relacionamento pessoal com Trump, esteve no Irã nesta segunda-feira para conversações, segundo a mídia iraniana. O Paquistão afirmou que a visita tinha como objetivo “promover a paz e a estabilidade regionais”, e uma fonte paquistanesa disse que Munir se reuniria com pessoas próximas ao líder supremo do Irã. Duas fontes paquistanesas afirmaram que Trump havia ligado para Munir na semana passada, e outra fonte disse que o principal pedido era fazer com que o Irã voltasse às negociações. A Casa Branca confirmou a ligação, mas não comentou sobre seu conteúdo. Os EUA e o Irã não realizam ataques aéreos contra suas forças militares há semanas, mas suas últimas negociações oficiais diretas para pôr fim ao conflito, que já dura seis meses, ocorreram em junho, e os ataques a embarcações no Estreito de Ormuz continuaram. Um projétil atingiu um petroleiro a oeste da cidade portuária saudita de Yanbu, no Mar Vermelho, nesta segunda-feira, causando um incêndio no convés principal, segundo informaram monitores de navegação da Maritime Trade Operations do Reino Unido. Um porta-voz dos houthis aliados do Irã, que no mês passado anunciaram que bloqueariam as exportações de petróleo sauditas desviadas para o Mar Vermelho a fim de evitar o Estreito de Ormuz, disse que haviam atacado uma embarcação na área. A companhia nacional de navegação da Arábia Saudita confirmou que uma de suas embarcações havia sido atacada.

item.title: Café dispara à medida que estoques de arábica na bolsa se aproximam da mínima de 26 anos
item.description: Os contratos futuros de café na bolsa ICE registraram forte alta nesta segunda-feira, com o arábica atingindo a maior cotação em mais de um mês, à medida que o período de notificação de entrega do primeiro contrato teve início com volumes reduzidos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de café na bolsa ICE registraram forte alta nesta segunda-feira, com o arábica atingindo a maior cotação em mais de um mês, à medida que o período de notificação de entrega do primeiro contrato teve início com volumes reduzidos. CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou com alta de 19 centavos, ou 5,9%, a US$3,4165 por libra-peso, após ter atingido anteriormente a maior cotação em seis semanas, de US$3,4255. O primeiro vencimento atingiu US$3,7795, o preço mais alto desde janeiro. * Os estoques de arábica certificados pela ICE continuaram a cair e agora estão próximos da mínima de 26 anos. * O corretor e consultor de café Mike Nugent disse que o período de notificação de entrega começou devagar, com apenas algumas dezenas de notificações. * "O mercado de curto prazo enviou uma mensagem clara: o café disponível em algum lugar não é necessariamente café disponível aqui, agora, em condições de entrega", disse ele. * O mercado invertido está precificando uma melhora na oferta no futuro, mas há dúvidas no mercado sobre a rapidez com que o café será transportado dos países produtores para os mercados consumidores, disseram os corretores. * Olhando para o futuro, espera-se que os preços do arábica caiam 8,8% até o final de 2026, já que o excedente de mercado para 2026/27 deve aumentar de 1,7 milhão para 8,2 milhões de sacas, de acordo com uma pesquisa da Reuters. * O preço do café robusta subiu 5,1%, para US$3.802 a tonelada. AÇÚCAR * O preço do açúcar bruto fechou em alta de 0,04 cent, ou 0,2%, a 17,65 centavos por libra-peso, após atingir uma máxima de 18,26 centavos na última quinta-feira, quando a Índia anunciou que permitiria a importação isenta de impostos de 1 milhão de toneladas métricas de açúcar bruto devido aos preços domésticos recordes. * A corretora Admis afirmou que os futuros de açúcar bruto na ICE, em seu pico na semana passada, haviam subido 27% em apenas três semanas, levando o mercado a uma correção moderada. A empresa acrescentou que há rumores de que os preços elevados tenham provocado vendas de hedge no Brasil, principal produtor. * Enquanto isso, na Índia, segundo maior produtor, a Associação Indiana de Usinas de Açúcar afirmou que a alta nos preços do açúcar indiano tem sido impulsionada por compras especulativas, e não por qualquer escassez real de oferta. * As chuvas diminuíram por enquanto no Brasil, permitindo que a colheita tenha avançado rapidamente, afirmou o corretor e consultor Michael McDougall. * O serviço de monitoramento de safras da União Europeia, o Mars, reduziu na segunda-feira suas previsões de rendimento da beterraba sacarina para 2026 em 11% em relação ao ano anterior, para 72,2 toneladas/ha. * O preço do açúcar branco caiu 2,8%, para US$535,90 por tonelada. CACAU * O preço de referência do cacau em Londres fechou em queda de £27, ou 0,6%, para £4.298 por tonelada. * O cacau em Nova York caiu 1,5%, para US$5.945 por tonelada. * O analista de cacau da StoneX, Lucca Bezzon, disse que o mercado passou por uma pequena correção técnica na segunda-feira, após os ganhos registrados na semana anterior. * Ele disse que tanto Gana quanto a Costa do Marfim anteciparam a safra oficial em um mês; portanto, a partir da próxima semana já deve haver alguns dados sobre a oferta da nova safra. * "O foco do mercado continua na nova safra 2026/27. Ainda há muita incerteza sobre a produção africana", disse ele, indicando que os volumes poderiam ficar cerca de 10% abaixo do ciclo anterior. (Reportagem de May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: US SEC sends subpoenas to Wall Street banks over Situational Awareness, NYT reports
item.description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has sent subpoenas to major Wall Street banks, seeking information about the trading of hedge fund Situational Awareness, the New York Times reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has sent subpoenas to major Wall Street banks, seeking information about the trading of hedge fund Situational Awareness, the New York Times reported on Monday. The requests included details on the AI-focused fund's communications with lenders about the leverage it was taking on, alongside the timings of its trades, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. Any investigation into the fund is at an early stages and there is no guarantee the probe will lead to fines or other punishment, the report added. The SEC and Situational Awareness did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Reuters could not independently verify the report. The hedge fund, run by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, sold the bulk of its portfolio to Citadel last month after losses in its tech holdings forced it to unwind most of its public equities portfolio.

item.title: Imagem de ato de Lula "vazio" mostra início do evento
item.description: Posts nas redes sociais mostram um registro feito no início do evento de lançamento da campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) à reeleição para alegar que o ato estava vazio.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Posts nas redes sociais mostram um registro feito no início do evento de lançamento da campanha do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) à reeleição para alegar que o ato estava vazio. “Agora sabemos por que Lula não autorizou que a USP fizesse a contagem de público no evento flopado. Mesmo fretando ônibus, não teve público e manipulam as imagens com IA”, diz uma publicação no Facebook com a foto. A imagem foi retirada de um vídeo publicado pela primeira-dama, Janja Lula da Silva, no Instagram no dia 16, quando Lula começou sua campanha em um evento no Estádio 1º de Maio, em São Bernardo do Campo (SP). A gravação foi compartilhada nos Stories, que são publicações temporárias, e, por isso, não está mais disponível no perfil da primeira-dama. Porém, o site Metrópoles replicou a filmagem , que mostra o estádio a partir de um helicóptero e com partes do gramado vazias. O ato estava marcado para começar às 9h , mas o palco só foi ocupado por volta das 9h30min , como mostra a transmissão ao vivo feita pelo PT no YouTube. Segundo a ferramenta Suncalc , que detecta o movimento solar, Janja gravou as imagens por volta das 9h50min, horário em que o sol estava atrás do palco, projetando as sombras para sudoeste, na direção da rua Olavo Bilac . Fotos da Reuters mostram que quando a primeira-dama discursou, por volta das 11h10min , apoiadores ocupavam a área do estádio que aparecia vazia no vídeo feito do helicóptero. A reportagem não registrou imagens que capturassem o público durante o pronunciamento de Lula. Segundo estimativas do PT, o evento reuniu cerca de 40 mil pessoas. O Poder360 e o Monitor do Debate Político da Universidade de São Paulo (USP) disseram que a campanha de Lula não permitiu o sobrevoo de drones no evento, inviabilizando a contagem independente do público no local. VEREDICTO Enganoso. A imagem que mostra o lançamento da campanha de Lula "vazio" foi feita no início do evento. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: US plans to revoke tourism and business visas of up to 200,000 foreigners, AP reports
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States, the Associated Press reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States, the Associated Press reported on Monday. The report cited State Department documents obtained by AP and two U.S. officials. If the move materialized, it would be the largest single mass revocation of visas in U.S. history, according to AP. The State Department is expected to announce in the coming weeks the revocation of so-called B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026 whose holders have sought asylum or are now seeking asylum, the report added, saying the action will be coordinated with the Department of Homeland Security. The B1 and B2 [USN:L4N43Y02H TEXT:"visas are issued"] for business and tourism travel. The visa revocations would not necessarily result in immediate deportation, the AP report said, citing officials. Most of those with asylum cases currently pending would be re-categorized but would lose their status as business or tourism travelers, the report said. Earlier on Monday, Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau alleged on X that the American immigration system "has long been swamped by frivolous asylum claims." The DHS referred questions to the State Department, which did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The State Department said earlier this month it has [USN:L6N4470TW TEXT:"revoked more than 175,000 visas"] from foreign nationals under the Trump administration. Trump has pursued an aggressive [USN:L4N44L066 TEXT:"immigration crackdown"] that he says is aimed at improving domestic security. Rights groups say the crackdown has violated free speech and due process rights and created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about [USN:L4N3ZU0AN TEXT:"racial profiling"].

item.title: Fentanyl, a Reagan ad and a near deal: Trump's trade war with Canada
item.description: Canada and the United States have been locked in a tariff war since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025.
item.dc:creator: Promit Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: Canada and the United States have been locked in a tariff war since U.S. President Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025. The dispute has impacted steel, aluminum, automobiles, lumber and other industries, prompting Canadian retaliation and repeated rounds of negotiations and tariff threats. Talks to avert 50% U.S. tariffs on around $20 billion of Canadian goods broke down late on Friday, spurring a pledge from Prime Minister Mark Carney to retaliate. Here is a timeline of key developments in the trade dispute that have upended the decades-old relationship: FEBRUARY 1, 2025 - TRUMP ANNOUNCES TARIFFS ON CANADA Trump announced tariffs on Canadian goods to take effect on February 4. Canada responded by announcing a C$155 billion retaliatory tariff package, with duties on an initial C$30 billion of U.S. imports. FEBRUARY 3, 2025 - TARIFFS PAUSED FOR 30 DAYS The United States agreed to pause the tariffs on Canada for 30 days; Canada suspended retaliation. FEBRUARY 10, 2025 - TRUMP TARGETS STEEL AND ALUMINUM Trump signed orders imposing 25% tariffs on steel and aluminum imports from all countries, including Canada, starting on March 12. MARCH 4, 2025 - U.S. TARIFFS TAKE EFFECT, CANADA RETALIATES U.S. tariffs of 25% on Canadian goods and 10% on Canadian energy products took effect. Canada retaliated with 25% tariffs on C$30 billion worth of U.S. products, including orange juice, peanut butter, wine, spirits, beer, coffee, appliances, apparel and motorcycles. MARCH 6, 2025 - U.S. GIVES USMCA-COMPLIANT GOODS A REPRIEVE Washington exempted imports compliant with the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement from the tariffs. Canada, under then Prime Minister Justin Trudeau, suspended a planned second wave of retaliation. MARCH 12-13, 2025 - METALS TARIFFS TRIGGER MORE CANADIAN RETALIATION U.S. tariffs of 25% on steel and aluminum imports took effect. Canada responded the following day with 25% tariffs on C$29.8 billion of U.S. goods, including steel and aluminum products, computers, servers, display monitors and sporting equipment. MARCH 26, 2025 - TRUMP ANNOUNCES 25% AUTO TARIFFS Trump ordered a 25% tariff on automobiles imported into the United States from April 3. For vehicles imported under the USMCA agreement, tariffs would apply only to the value of content not produced in the United States. APRIL 9, 2025 - AUTO TARIFF BATTLE INTENSIFIES Canada announced 25% counter-tariffs on non-CUSMA-compliant vehicles imported from the United States and on the non-Canadian and non-Mexican content of compliant vehicles. MAY 6, 2025 - CARNEY MEETS TRUMP Prime Minister Mark Carney made his first visit to the White House since becoming prime minister, seeking to reset relations. JUNE 3, 2025 - U.S. DOUBLES STEEL AND ALUMINUM TARIFFS The United States announced an increase in its tariffs on imported steel and aluminum to 50% from 25%. JUNE 16, 2025 - TRUMP AND CARNEY SET 30-DAY TARGET FOR A DEAL Carney and Trump met on the sidelines of the Group of Seven summit in Kananaskis, Alberta. JUNE 27-29, 2025 - DIGITAL TAX DERAILS TALKS, CANADA RETREATS Trump abruptly ended trade talks with Canada over its digital services tax, which was due to begin collecting payments from large technology companies. Two days later, Canada rescinded the tax in an effort to restart negotiations with Washington. JULY 31, 2025 - TRUMP RAISES TARIFF ON NON-USMCA GOODS TO 35% Trump signed an order increasing tariffs on Canadian products that did not qualify for USMCA preferential treatment to 35% from 25%. The White House linked the measures to what it said was Canada's failure to curb the flow of fentanyl into the United States, a claim that was not supported by official data. AUGUST 22, 2025 - CANADA REMOVES MOST RETALIATORY TARIFFS Carney announced Canada would remove retaliatory tariffs on a broad range of U.S. goods while keeping counter-tariffs on steel, aluminum and automobiles. SEPTEMBER 29, 2025 - U.S. ADDS SOFTWOOD LUMBER TARIFF Trump imposed an additional 10% tariff on Canadian softwood lumber, taking total U.S. levies on the product to more than 45%. OCTOBER 7, 2025 - CARNEY RETURNS TO WHITE HOUSE Carney met Trump in the Oval Office for a second time. OCTOBER 24, 2025 - TRUMP SUSPENDS TRADE TALKS Trump suspended trade negotiations with Canada over an advertisement aired by the Ontario government that used comments by former U.S. President Ronald Reagan criticizing tariffs. JUNE 2, 2026 - USTR IMPOSES 12.5% TARIFFS The office of the U.S. Trade Representative issued an order imposing an up to 12.5% tariff on 60 countries for failing to curb trade in goods made with forced labor, including Canada. Canada says it has always followed strict rules to restrict products from countries that used forced labor. JULY 1, 2026 - TRUMP DECLINES TO RENEW USMCA Trump declined to renew the continental free trade pact, subjecting it to annual reviews. JULY 20, 2026 - SECTION 338 Trump signed three proclamations invoking the Depression-era Section 338 Tariff Act to impose additional 50% tariffs on some $20 billion of Canadian goods such as Canadian wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods, and hockey equipment. The threat led to intensive engagements between the two sides as Canada sought to avert the tariffs. AUGUST 22, 2026 - TALKS BETWEEN U.S. AND CANADA COLLAPSE The U.S. imposed the 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods on Saturday after the two sides failed to reach a trade deal; Carney suspended trade talks, called back his negotiators from Washington and vowed dollar-for-dollar retaliation. AUGUST 24, 2026 - TRUMP ANNOUNCES NEW AUTO TARIFFS On Monday, Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks and automotive parts to come into effect from January 1, 2027.

item.title: Peso mexicano se repliega tras tocar máximos desde mayo 2024, bolsa sube por cuarta sesión
item.description: El peso mexicano se debilitó el lunes, apartándose de su mejor nivel en más de dos años, ante un repunte global del dólar y una renovada cautela sobre el entorno comercial de Norteamérica, en el marco de la revisión del tratado regional de negocios, TMEC.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano se debilitó el lunes, apartándose de su mejor nivel en más de dos años, ante un [USN:L1N44L0TA TEXT:"repunte global del dólar"] y una renovada cautela sobre el entorno comercial de Norteamérica, en el marco de la revisión del tratado regional de negocios, TMEC. La sesión también estuvo marcada por datos locales de [USN:L1N44L0F9 TEXT:"economía"] e [USN:L1N44L0G5 TEXT:"inflación"], al inicio de una semana centrada en el simposio de Jackson Hole. Los mercados seguirán además las cifras estadounidenses de inflación PCE y PIB, además del reporte trimestral de Banco de México. * La moneda local cotizaba en 16.9529 unidades por dólar en la recta final de los negocios, con una depreciación de 0.34%. El viernes había llegado a 16.8824, su nivel más fuerte desde mayo de 2024. * "Esta corrección podría ser una primera señal de que el tipo de cambio podría ajustarse nuevamente, lo que implicaría que regrese a cotizar por encima de los 17 pesos por dólar", dijo Banco Base. * El [USN:L1N44L0TA TEXT:"dólar estadounidense"] avanzó después de que el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump anunciara una ampliación de las sanciones contra Irán, mientras los operadores seguían de cerca los planes del Tesoro estadounidense para recomprar deuda de largo plazo. * La presión sobre el peso también reflejó preocupaciones sobre el comercio regional. [USN:L6N44J02G TEXT:"Estados Unidos"] impuso durante el fin de semana aranceles a algunos productos canadienses, luego de que fracasaran las negociaciones entre ambos países. * El episodio añadió incertidumbre para México en el contexto de la revisión del TMEC, un proceso que los inversionistas vigilan por sus posibles efectos sobre las exportaciones y los flujos de inversión. * En el frente local, se dio a conocer que el [USN:L1N44L0F9 TEXT:"Producto Interno Bruto"] se expandió en el segundo trimestre a un ritmo ligeramente inferior al previsto inicialmente. * En tanto, la inflación general de la [USN:L1N44L0G5 TEXT:"primera quincena de agosto"] aumentó menos de lo esperado. En contraste, el componente subyacente se desaceleró de forma inesperada, una señal relevante para las expectativas sobre la política monetaria. * La bolsa mexicana revirtió sus pérdidas y cerró en tono positivo. El índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) avanzó un marginal 0.06% a 65,770.85 puntos, en su cuarta jornada de ganancias. * Las acciones de la embotelladora Coca-Cola FEMSA (KOFUBL.MX) encabezaron las alzas, con un 3.12% más a 194.94 pesos. Les siguieron los títulos de la prestamista Gentera (GENTERA.MX) , que sumaron un 2.92% a 39.50 pesos. * En el mercado secundario de deuda, el rendimiento del bono gubernamental a 10 años descendió un punto base a un 9.22%, igual que la tasa a 20 años que terminó la jornada en un 9.69%.

item.title: US judge dismisses legal challenge to Trump's offshore drilling expansion
item.description: An Alaska federal judge on Monday threw out a lawsuit by environmental groups challenging President Donald Trump’s move to allow offshore drilling along broad swaths of previously protected coastline.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: An Alaska federal judge on Monday threw out a [USN:L2N3PA0WB TEXT:"lawsuit by environmental groups"] challenging President Donald Trump ’s move to allow offshore drilling along broad swaths of previously protected coastline. U.S. District Judge Sharon L. Gleason found the lawsuit by groups, including the Northern Alaska Environmental Center, was premature because drilling was not imminent in federal waters that were placed off-limits by Trump’s predecessors. Gleason did not rule on whether presidents have legal authority to [USN:L1N3O403L TEXT:"undo their predecessors’ withdrawal"] of coastal areas from drilling and left the door open for the groups to refile their lawsuit. Earthjustice, an advocacy group whose attorneys filed the lawsuit, said in a statement that the group still believes Trump's actions were unlawful and that it would refile its case should federal officials expand offshore drilling. "We’re disappointed the court found that offshore drilling activities are not imminent," the group said in a statement. "This administration has been doing everything in its power to open our coasts to fossil fuel development. We continue to maintain that President Trump’s attempt to open withdrawn areas for oil leasing is unlawful, and we intend to pursue those claims if and when offshore activities are on the horizon." The U.S. Department of Justice did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Former Democratic President Joe Biden banned new offshore oil and gas development along most U.S. coastlines ahead of Trump taking office, though the move was considered mostly symbolic because it did not impact areas where drilling was already underway and mainly covered zones lacking important development prospects. Trump, a Republican, sought to undo that move as part of a flurry of executive orders within hours of his inauguration aimed at boosting the nation's already record-high oil and gas production and unwinding Biden's efforts to address climate change. The environmental groups said in their February 2025 lawsuit that Trump lacked authority to undo the protections, and that allowing drilling in those areas would have “significant, wide-ranging adverse impacts” on endangered species, sensitive ecosystems and local Native American communities.

item.title: Vídeo usa falas de Lula fora de contexto para acusá-lo de ofender pobres
item.description: Um vídeo que circula nas redes sociais reúne uma série de cortes de falas do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva para alegar que ele proferiu discursos ofensivos contra pessoas pobres. Na realidade, os pronunciamentos completos mostram que Lula se referia a pensamentos que atribui a terceiros.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo que circula nas redes sociais reúne uma série de cortes de falas do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva para alegar que ele proferiu discursos ofensivos contra pessoas pobres. Na realidade, os pronunciamentos completos mostram que Lula se referia a pensamentos que atribui a terceiros. O conteúdo checado foi compartilhado no Facebook e no Instagram. No primeiro vídeo, Lula diz que "na época da eleição, pobre tem um valor desgraçado". É uma fala do mês passado, e a íntegra, disponível no canal do UOL no YouTube e no perfil do Instituto Lula no Instagram , mostra que ele fazia uma crítica a políticos que, segundo ele, só "gostam de falar com os pobres na época da eleição". No segundo, Lula afirma que "pobre é imbecil, é ignorante". É um trecho de uma entrevista ao Podpah em dezembro de 2021, na qual o presidente falava sobre as críticas à criação do Bolsa Família. "Quando nós criamos o Bolsa Família, o que que a elite brasileira falava? 'Ah, o Lula está criando vagabundo' (...). É a falta de crença no povo pobre. É a falta de respeito às pessoas pobres. Porque todo mundo acha que pobre é imbecil, é ignorante", disse. Na seguinte, o presidente diz que "só na época da eleição é que pobre vira importante" e que "na época da eleição, o pobre é mais importante do que o rico, porque o pobre é maioria e tem voto". É um discurso de maio deste ano, e a fala completa, publicada pelo Poder360 no YouTube , deixa claro que Lula estava condenando políticos que, segundo ele, "estão pouco ligando para o povo pobre", que seriam lembrados apenas em período eleitoral. No corte seguinte, o presidente fala que "pobre não precisa estudar" e que "nasceu só para trabalhar". A Reuters já verificou este conteúdo e mostrou que Lula rebatia o pensamento de que pessoas pobres não precisam estudar. "Aqui demorou 420 anos para fazer a primeira universidade. Por que será que acontecia isso? É porque pobre não precisa estudar", afirmou. O outro vídeo mostra Lula dizendo que "rico, quando vai pegar dinheiro, pega logo um monte, mas o pobre precisa de pouco dinheiro". É um trecho do discurso do presidente no lançamento do programa Gás do Povo, em setembro de 2025, e a íntegra foi publicada pelo Poder360 no YouTube . Lula falava sobre distribuição de renda e a necessidade de o Estado atender aos mais pobres. "Um país, para dar certo, precisa garantir que muitos tenham pouco dinheiro. Para dar errado, precisa garantir que poucos tenham muito dinheiro. Se poucos tiverem muito dinheiro, significa que a maioria não tem. E se muitos tiverem pouco dinheiro, todo mundo tendo um pouco, a gente não vai precisar criar programa de dar gás de graça", disse. As imagens seguintes são do político dizendo: "Será que vocês não percebem? Pobre não nasceu para estudar, pobre nasceu para trabalhar. Estudar é filho de rico, que pode estudar na França (...)". Trata-se da sequência da fala mencionada acima, checada anteriormente pela Reuters . Depois, o conteúdo checado reproduz Lula afirmando que "pobre é pobre, tem que trabalhar. Pobre é pobre, a gente ganha o voto de pobre na época da eleição, para que cuidar de pobre?". A Reuters também já verificou posts que usavam o mesmo corte, mostrando que o presidente se referia ao que atribuiu à opinião da "elite conservadora". No penúltimo clipe, o presidente diz que "pobre não tem que aprender, pobre tem que trabalhar; negro não tem que aprender, negro tem que trabalhar". A Reuters também checou conteúdos semelhantes e identificou que se trata de um discurso de Lula na campanha eleitoral de 2022. O registro completo, publicado no canal da Pontifícia Universidade Católica de São Paulo (PUC-SP) no YouTube , mostra que Lula criticava o que chamou de "mentalidade escravista" da elite política brasileira. Por fim, o vídeo mostra um apoiador falando para Lula que "o maior orgulho que eu tive de você foi o dia que você foi preso, companheiro". O conteúdo reproduz somente um corte da fala do homem, que, na realidade, disse: "Presidente, o maior orgulho que eu tive de você foi o dia em que você foi preso, com a cabeça levantada, como quem não devia nada a ninguém. E não devia mesmo". O momento, registrado durante a entrega de títulos de assentamentos em março do ano passado, foi publicado pela rádio Itatiaia no YouTube . VEREDICTO Enganoso. O conteúdo checado reproduz cortes de discursos de Lula como se o presidente tivesse ofendido pessoas pobres. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: US colleges win chance to appeal class action order in financial aid lawsuit
item.description: A U.S. appeals court on Monday said it will hear a challenge to a judge’s order that allowed a class action to move forward against Cornell and several other elite U.S. universities alleging they colluded to reduce student financial aid.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: A U.S. appeals court on Monday said it will hear a challenge to a judge’s order that allowed a class action to move forward against Cornell and several other elite U.S. universities alleging they colluded to reduce student financial aid. Here are the details: The Chicago-based 7th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals granted a request from Cornell and several other schools to immediately appeal an order that allowed students to band together in the lawsuit to sue as a class. U.S. District Judge Matthew Kennelly in June certified a class of more than 220,000 students who attended the schools over 20 years. The universities said potential class action damages could exceed $2 billion, stemming from an automatic provision in U.S. antitrust law that triples jury awards. The lawsuit filed in 2022 in federal court in Chicago [USN:L6N3YE0AY TEXT:"alleged"] 17 of the country’s top schools suppressed competition for financial aid and favored wealthy students in admissions. The universities’ lawyers in their appeal said Kennelly based his ruling on class certification “solely on the flawed work of plaintiffs’ expert.” In its order on Monday, the appeals court said its review will be “limited to the sole issue of whether the district court adequately analyzed expert testimony related to the question of common proof of antitrust impact.” Kennelly had scheduled a trial to start in November. Cornell declined to comment. A lead lawyer for the plaintiffs did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Twelve universities, including Brown, Yale and Columbia, have already agreed to settlements with the plaintiffs worth nearly [USN:L2N3OF024 TEXT:"$320 million"]. All the defendants, including those that have settled, have denied any wrongdoing.
