item.content:encoded: Tesla has stopped selling premium solar roof tiles on its website, nearly a decade after CEO Elon Musk launched the product as a more attractive alternative to panels. Tesla's solar roof url now redirects to a solar panels offering. Discontinuation of the product was first reported by Electrek last week. Tesla did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Musk [USN:L1N1CZ012 TEXT:"unveiled"] the roof tiles in 2016 as Tesla sought to acquire SolarCity, the solar installer run by his cousins. The company in 2021 had targeted 1,000 installations per week, but industry estimates said the actual figure was [USN:L4N3613UE TEXT:"far less"]. Tesla's solar strategy has shifted to traditional panels, which it produces at its factory in Buffalo, New York, and began delivering to residential customers this year. Musk still has big ambitions in solar. Tesla filed plans in Texas this month for a $10.1 billion solar-cell factory outside Houston that would create 9,712 permanent jobs.

item.title: Tribunal apelación FIA tendrá la última palabra sobre el podio de Gasly en el Gran Premio de Mónaco
item.description: El tribunal de apelación de la Fórmula 1 se reunirá el martes en París para decidir de una vez por todas quién quedó tercero en el Gran Premio de Mónaco, más de dos meses después de la carrera.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: El tribunal de apelación de la Fórmula 1 se reunirá el martes en París para decidir de una vez por todas quién quedó tercero en el Gran Premio de Mónaco, más de dos meses después de la carrera. Pierre Gasly, de Alpine, fue tercero el 7 de junio, pero fue relegado al séptimo puesto cuando los comisarios le impusieron tras la carrera dos sanciones de cinco segundos por exceso de velocidad en el pit lane, lo que permitió a Isack Hadjar, de Red Bull, ascender al último escalón del podio. Esa decisión fue revocada el 12 de junio, después de que los comisarios aceptaran las pruebas presentadas por Alpine —propiedad de Renault— de que se había producido un error de cronometraje y retiraran las sanciones, con lo que Hadjar devolvió el trofeo a Gasly. Ante las advertencias de algunos expertos del paddock de que el veredicto había abierto la caja de Pandora, McLaren y Red Bull recurrieron ante el tribunal internacional el 16 de junio. McLaren planteó sus objeciones después de que Oscar Piastri, que cayó del cuarto al quinto puesto tras la reinstauración de Gasly, recibiera sanciones durante la carrera por la misma infracción, partiendo de la base de que era inevitable, aunque él estaba seguro de no haber excedido la velocidad. A diferencia de Gasly, que no cumplió sus sanciones durante la carrera y al que se le añadió un tiempo que podía eliminarse, Piastri no tuvo recurso alguno, y el tiempo perdido en boxes también tuvo un efecto en cadena en la forma de correr del australiano a partir de ese momento. El jefe del equipo, Andrea Stella, declaró durante el Gran Premio de los Países Bajos del fin de semana —ganado por Lando Norris, de McLaren— que la apelación tenía un doble objetivo. "Creemos que el proceso que tuvo lugar tras la carrera de Mónaco debe revisarse porque, desde el punto de vista de la equidad para todos los competidores, el hecho de que se retirara la sanción plantea algunos motivos de preocupación significativos", afirmó. "El segundo aspecto es el interés de McLaren. También nos vimos penalizados de forma sustancial por haber cumplido una sanción que no era apelable y esto incluso nos costó puntos en el campeonato", añadió. La FIA indicó que la audiencia, a la que no asistirán el público ni los medios de comunicación por motivos de confidencialidad, se celebrará en la sede de la FIA y que la decisión se publicará lo antes posible.

item.title: Bolsas europeas se mantienen estables, mercados evalúan tensiones con Irán y esperan datos económicos
item.description: Las bolsas europeas se mantuvieron estables este lunes, mientras los mercados seguían de cerca la evolución de la situación entre Estados Unidos e Irán y se preparaban para una semana repleta de datos económicos que podrían ofrecer nuevas pistas sobre la trayectoria de la política monetaria del Banco Central Europeo.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Utkarsh Hathi
item.content:encoded: Las bolsas europeas se mantuvieron estables este lunes, mientras los mercados seguían de cerca la evolución de la situación entre Estados Unidos e Irán y se preparaban para una semana repleta de datos económicos que podrían ofrecer nuevas pistas sobre la trayectoria de la política monetaria del Banco Central Europeo. Los inversores se preparaban para conocer los detalles de unas posibles sanciones secundarias más duras de Estados Unidos contra países con vínculos comerciales con Irán, cuyo anuncio se espera por parte del secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent. Por otra parte, el jefe del Ejército de Pakistán se encuentra en Teherán para intentar que Irán vuelva a la mesa de negociaciones. "En estos momentos hay muchas incógnitas en torno a esto (las sanciones)", afirmó Chris Beauchamp, analista jefe de mercados de IG Group. "Si se da una situación en la que la medida de Estados Unidos se interpreta como una amenaza para la economía iraní y esta responde de la única forma que puede, tomando medidas en el estrecho de Ormuz, sería especialmente negativo para los mercados europeos". El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) cerró sin cambios, en 654,21 puntos. La amenaza de sanciones se suma a los temores de una inflación prolongada que se apoderaron de los mercados mundiales la semana pasada, cuando los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos alcanzaron su máximo en varias décadas, en medio de las persistentes tensiones en Oriente Medio que han mantenido elevados los precios del petróleo. Entre los sectores, las acciones de viajes y ocio, que consumen mucha energía (.SXTP) , lideraron las subidas, con un alza del 1,7%, mientras que el crudo Brent bajaba un 1,9%. Las acciones de los medios de comunicación (.SXPP) y de los bienes personales y para el hogar (.SXQP) subieron un 1,4%. El índice de referencia STOXX 600 ha retrocedido en las últimas semanas tras alcanzar máximos históricos a principios de este mes, en un repunte impulsado por los resultados empresariales, mientras las preocupaciones por la inflación han pasado a primer plano. Los mercados monetarios están descontando una política más restrictiva por parte del Banco Central Europeo, apostando por que las tensiones geopolíticas podrían mantener elevadas las presiones sobre los precios e impulsar el tipo de depósito hasta cerca del 3% a finales de 2027.

item.title: FIA appeal court to have final say on Gasly's Monaco GP podium
item.description: Formula One's international court of appeal will meet in Paris on Tuesday to decide once and for all who finished third in the Monaco Grand Prix, more than two months after the event.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Formula One's international court of appeal will meet in Paris on Tuesday to decide once and for all who finished third in the Monaco Grand Prix, more than two months after the event. Alpine's Pierre Gasly finished third in the Mediterranean principality on June 7 but was [USN:L1N42F05I TEXT:"demoted to seventh"] when two five-second penalties for pit-lane speeding were applied by stewards post-race, with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar promoted to third and spraying the champagne. That decision was [USN:L6N42K0N7 TEXT:"overturned on June 12"], after stewards accepted Renault-owned Alpine's evidence that there had been a timekeeping error and removed the penalties, with Hadjar [USN:L6N42X114 TEXT:"handing the trophy back"] to Gasly. With some paddock insiders warning that the verdict [USN:L6N42L04D TEXT:"opened a can of worms"], McLaren and Red Bull [USN:L6N42O0YF TEXT:"appealed to the international court "]on June 16. McLaren took issue after Oscar Piastri, who dropped from fourth to fifth following Gasly's reinstatement, took penalties during the race for the same offence under the assumption it was unavoidable even though he was sure he had not been speeding. Unlike Gasly, who did not serve his penalties during the race and had time added on that could be removed, Piastri had no recourse with the time lost in the pits also having a knock-on effect on how the Australian raced after that. Team boss Andrea Stella said at the weekend's [USN:L6N44K04A TEXT:"Dutch Grand Prix"], won by McLaren's Lando Norris, that the appeal had a double intent. "We think that the process that happened after the race in Monaco needs to be reviewed because from a (standpoint of) fairness for all competitors, the fact that the penalty was removed introduces some significant elements of concern," he said. "The second aspect is the interest of McLaren. We got also materially penalised for having served a penalty that is not appealable and this even cost us points in the championship," added the Italian. "So there's a general interest for Formula One and the sport and the integrity of the sport, and there's a material interest for McLaren in terms of our championship impact." The FIA said the hearing, without public or media present for reasons of confidentiality, would be at the FIA headquarters with a decision published as soon as possible.

item.title: Law firm Paul Weiss taps new Supreme Court practice head after Shanmugam exit
item.description: Law firm Paul Weiss has hired William Jay to lead its Supreme Court and appellate litigation practice, filling the role after the group's prominent head Kannon Shanmugam left for another firm earlier this year.
item.dc:creator: Sara Merken
item.content:encoded: Law firm Paul Weiss has hired William Jay to lead its Supreme Court and appellate litigation practice, filling the role after the group's prominent head Kannon Shanmugam left for another firm earlier this year. Jay, who has argued 19 cases before the U.S. Supreme Court, joins Paul Weiss as a Washington, D.C.-based partner, the firm said on Monday. He has represented clients including Teva Pharmaceuticals, Varsity Brands and B&B Hardware. Shanmugam, who previously led the Supreme Court practice at Paul Weiss, [USN:L6N4161HM TEXT:"departed"] with Masha Hansford in April to launch a new practice at law firm Davis Polk. Jay practiced at Goodwin for 14 years. He previously worked as an assistant to the Solicitor General. Earlier in his career he was a clerk to former U.S. Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia. Jay told Reuters that he was eager to join Paul Weiss as the New York firm grows its litigation department. Paul Weiss has hired a handful of litigation partners this year, including former U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission deputy enforcement director Antonia Apps in February. The firm has also seen litigator departures, including a pair of partners who joined Linklaters in July.

item.title: Hyundai Motor's union reaches tentative wage deal with management, Yonhap reports
item.description: Hyundai Motor's South Korean union reached a tentative agreement with management on a 100,000 won ($72.31) monthly base salary increase, Yonhap News Agency reported on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hyundai Motor's (005380.KS) South Korean union reached a tentative agreement with management on a 100,000 won ($72.31) monthly base salary increase, Yonhap News Agency reported on Tuesday. The deal comes after the union [USN:L1N44I02F TEXT:"staged its first full strike"] in a decade on Friday after wage talks stalled, as it sought a higher retirement age and job protections against artificial intelligence and automation. According to the Yonhap report, the tentative agreement includes a base salary increase plus a performance bonus and welfare points. From next year until 2028, 500 new technical workers will be hired, the report added. Hyundai Motor did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. Production at Hyundai's largest automobile factory in Ulsan city would have been suspended if the two sides had not reached a deal. The Ulsan plant has an annual capacity to produce about 1.5 million vehicles, accounting for roughly a quarter of Hyundai's total output. The union had demanded the company set aside 30% of net income for bonuses and guarantee job security, raising concerns over growing adoption of robotics and artificial intelligence on assembly lines. The world's third-largest automaker, which is also developing [USN:L1N43I027 TEXT:"humanoid robots"], appears to be planning to replace human workers with new technologies, a union leader said. "We already see lots of robots deployed in the factories," Kim Jin-wook, head of external relations for Hyundai's union, told Reuters. "We are demanding management increase new hires, as the company is trying to reduce headcounts." ($1 = 1,382.8900 won)

item.title: US removes Syria from terrorism sponsor list, lifting major investment obstacle
item.description: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism on Monday, lifting what Damascus says was the last major impediment to investing in the country as Washington deepens ties to the new Syrian government.
item.dc:creator: Feras Dalatey
item.content:encoded: The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism on Monday, lifting what Damascus says was the last major impediment to investing in the country as Washington deepens ties to the new Syrian government. The removal, posted on the U.S. Treasury's website, took effect after a 45-day congressional review period triggered when Trump formally notified Congress on July 8 of his intention to rescind the designation. “These actions were all taken in recognition of the positive actions taken and further commitments by the Syrian government under President Ahmed al-Sharaa to fully distance Syria from acts of international terrorism,” U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement. Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani [USN:L8N44J06U TEXT:"told Reuters"] on Saturday that the government hoped removing what he called the "last obstacle" would help reconnect Syria to the global financial and economic system and boost investment. "There is no longer any obstacle to investment, doing business and rebuilding economic life in Syria," he said. Syria had been on the list since 1979, when Washington accused the government of former President Hafez al-Assad of supporting militant groups. The designation remained throughout the rule of his son Bashar al-Assad, who was toppled by rebels led by current President Ahmed al-Sharaa in December 2024. CUBA, IRAN, NORTH KOREA REMAIN Monday's announcement also removed the designation of the Nusrah Front as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist organization, leaving Cuba, Iran and North Korea as the three countries designated by Washington as state sponsors of terrorism. The designation carries restrictions on U.S. foreign assistance, defense exports and sales, certain dual-use items and financial transactions, and had remained a major deterrent for banks and investors even after Washington dismantled its broader sanctions program on Syria. Trump's administration terminated comprehensive U.S. sanctions on Syria in July 2025, while maintaining targeted sanctions against Assad and his associates, rights abusers, drug traffickers, Islamic State and al Qaeda affiliates and Iranian proxies. The U.S. Treasury has since said American financial institutions can provide services to Syria, process payments involving Syrian banks and establish correspondent banking relationships with them, provided sanctioned parties are not involved. But the terrorism designation remained a source of legal and compliance risk for firms considering entering Syria, whose government is seeking billions of dollars in investment to rebuild after nearly 14 years of war. Signs of interest had grown ahead of the removal. Syria's finance ministry said this month that Finance Minister Mohammad Yisr Barnieh held talks with Bank of America (BAC.N) executives over potential cooperation and Syria's reintegration into the international financial system. Bank officials expressed willingness to visit Syria and continue discussions, according to the ministry. Mastercard (MA.N) has gone further, announcing in May that it was working with QNB Group (QNBK.QA) and Syria's central bank to prepare infrastructure for international card payments in the country. The company has described itself as an early investor in Syria and said it wants to help connect Syrian consumers and businesses to global payment networks. CONTINUED COOPERATION Trump notified Congress of his decision after meeting Sharaa in Ankara in July, telling the Syrian president in a letter seen by Reuters that he [USN:S0N3Y802F TEXT:"had promised"] to "remove all barriers" preventing Syria from rebuilding. The delisting also followed months of negotiations between Damascus and Washington over Syria's economic and foreign policy. Reuters [USN:L6N43U0ZX TEXT:"reported"] this month that Damascus agreed to drastically reduce imports of Russian oil during discussions with Washington over lifting the terrorism designation, according to three sources familiar with the talks. Trump has increasingly embraced Sharaa, the former commander of al Qaeda's Nusra Front who broke ties with the global jihadist network in 2016 and led the rebel coalition that overthrew Assad. Washington has praised cooperation by Sharaa's government against Islamic State and said easing restrictions is intended to give Syria an opportunity to stabilise, attract investment and rebuild.

item.title: Trump bought shares in Elon Musk's SpaceX in June, financial disclosure shows
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump invested as much as $50,000 in Elon Musk's SpaceX in June, according to a public financial disclosure, giving him a financial stake in a major government contractor run by his former adviser.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Rozen
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump invested as much as $50,000 in Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) in June, according to a public financial disclosure, giving him a financial stake in a major government contractor run by his former adviser. He bought between $15,001 and $50,000 in shares on June 23, according to a financial disclosure signed by him on August 12 and made public on August 22. The purchase was part of more than 1,000 stock trades the president made in June. SpaceX [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"priced"] the biggest-ever U.S. IPO on June 12, valuing the space, satellite and AI provider at $1.77 trillion. In a statement to Reuters, White House spokesman Davis Ingle said that third-party financial institutions independently manage the president's portfolio and replicate "recognized indexes, such as the Schwab 1000." "Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold," Ingle said in the statement. Trump's investment in SpaceX adds a new financial link between the president and Musk's rocket company at a time when the administration is making decisions that could affect the firm's fortunes. SpaceX is a U.S. military [USN:L1N3P10ZT TEXT:"contractor,"] and often seeks [USN:L1N43U12L TEXT:"approvals"] from federal agencies. Trump on Thursday [USN:S0N3ZQ02C TEXT:"directed"] his team to help drastically increase the number of U.S. commercial space launches. SpaceX is a dominant player in that sector. U.S. Small Business Administration leader and Trump cabinet member Kelly Loeffler earned millions from SpaceX's IPO, Reuters previously [USN:L6N43H172 TEXT:"reported"]. Loeffler first invested in xAI, Musk’s AI and social media firm that has since [USN:L4N3YY1U7 TEXT:"merged"] with SpaceX. She invested again after Trump nominated her to lead the SBA. Her first investment in xAI would have been worth between $7 million and $2.6 billion on the day of the IPO, depending on the exact amount she invested and the date she made it, said Franco Granda, analyst at data provider PitchBook. The second investment would have been worth between $2.2 million and $25.4 million that day, he said. Reuters could not immediately determine the precise amount of Trump's investment because federal officials use ranges to declare the value of their assets on their financial disclosure forms.

item.title: Italy regulator clears Ludoil's acquisition of Sicilian oil refiner
item.description: Italy's competition authority has cleared the acquisition of Sicily-based oil refiner ISAB by energy group Ludoil, the watchdog said on Monday, opening the way for a local company to control one fifth of the country's refining capacity.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy's competition authority has cleared the [USN:L8N41Q1HU TEXT:"acquisition"] of Sicily-based oil refiner ISAB by energy group Ludoil, the watchdog said on Monday, opening the way for a local company to control one fifth of the country's refining capacity. Ludoil agreed in May to buy 51% of ISAB from Cypriot private equity fund G.O.I. Energy, subject to several conditions. The antitrust regulator said that the transaction would not hamper competition in the Italian market for refined products in a significant way, adding it would not open a full investigation on the acquisition. The refiner is linked to an exclusive long-term contract with global commodity trader Trafigura until 2033, the watchdog said in its document, revealing interesting details regarding its business. The supply and offtake agreement commits ISAB to sell approximately 90% of its refined petroleum products to Trafigura while Trafigura supplies ISAB with crude oil and the other raw materials required for refining, the competition authority said.

item.title: Israeli fire kills two young children in Gaza, medics say
item.description: Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed two young children and at least two other Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Monday, health officials in the territory said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed two young children and at least two other Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Monday, health officials in the territory said. Medics and relatives said 10-year-old Amal Abu Khater was hit by a bullet in her back while she was eating inside her family's tent in the enclave's southern city of Khan Younis. The fire came from Israeli forces to the east, they added. The Israeli military said it was not aware of any incident involving a 10-year-old girl. A four-year-old boy and another Palestinian were killed in separate Israeli airstrikes on a house in Bureij refugee camp and a road in Khan Younis, medics said. Earlier on Monday, another Israeli airstrike killed one person and wounded another at a tent in Deir Al-Balah in the central Gaza Strip, medics said. The Israeli military said that strike in Deir Al-Balah targeted a Hamas militant, but did not specifically respond to questions about the other two reported attacks in Khan Younis and Bureij. More than 1,280 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since a ceasefire took effect last October , according to Gazan health officials, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed. Hamas accuses Israel of violating the ceasefire and undermining efforts to implement a broader plan by U.S. President Donald Trump to end the Gaza conflict, which also includes Israeli withdrawals and Hamas disarmament. Israel says its strikes aimed to thwart imminent attacks by Hamas and other Gaza militants. The Israeli military issued two separate evacuation orders in Beach refugee camp and Deir Al-Balah in northern and central Gaza Strip before it carried out airstrikes in the two areas, without reports of casualties, residents and medics said. It also bombed a desalination plant in the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood in Gaza City, at a time when the enclave is suffering water shortages, residents and Hamas said. An Israeli military spokesperson said the military had carried out strikes on several Hamas weapons storage sites throughout the day, including two inside mosques. The spokesperson said that among the sites targeted on Monday was one located adjacent to a desalination facility. The spokesperson said the military had not targeted the desalination facility and did not say whether or not it had been damaged in the strike.

item.title: Gang attack on hillside town near Haiti's capital leaves 30 dead
item.description: At least 30 people were killed in a gang raid in the neighborhood of Kenscoff near Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, Kenscoff's mayor Jean Massillon told Reuters on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 30 people were killed in a gang raid in the neighborhood of Kenscoff near Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, Kenscoff's mayor Jean Massillon told Reuters on Monday. Kenscoff is a hillside town overlooking Port-au-Prince has seen frequent gang attacks over the last couple of years. Rights groups have reported mass killings, rapes, arson and kidnappings, forcing thousands to flee their homes. Haitian rights group RNDDH estimated 30 to 40 people had been killed and 15 to 20 wounded in the overnight raid, which began around 10:30 p.m. local time (0230 GMT), but warned it was still difficult to assess a complete tally. Haiti's prime minister's office on Monday afternoon decried the "heinous attack", noting all security forces were on high alert and reinforcements were being deployed. "Kenscoff will not be abandoned," it said in a statement. "The government's authority will be restored, without weakness and without delay, throughout all of Kenscoff." Haiti's national police did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The community occupies a strategic position overlooking routes into Petion-Ville - home to several embassies, upscale hotels and the temporary seat of government - as well as routes from the capital into southern parts of the country. Local media said several houses were set on fire, including the home of Jean William Pape, a leading public health expert in Haiti. The attack occurred as the U.N.-backed Gang Suppression Force, which is mandated to help police fight gangs and replace an underfunded and ineffectual predecessor, plans to reach a full capacity of more than 5,500 troops by fall this year.

item.title: Browns to open season with Deshaun Watson as QB1
item.description: New Browns head coach Todd Monken opted to stay the course in Cleveland and will start Deshaun Watson at quarterback in Week 1 of the regular season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Browns head coach Todd Monken opted to stay the course in Cleveland and will start Deshaun Watson at quarterback in Week 1 of the regular season. "Took in the full body of work over the course of offseason to training camp to the games and the joint practice, and ultimately, felt like to start the season on the road, Deshaun gave us the best chance to move the ball and score points," Monken said Monday. "And that's really what it's about. I felt that way going into the last game, but wasn't sure. And after we talked as a staff and after we re-looked at everything, we're going to let it rip." Watson and Shedeur Sanders competed for the starting job in training camp, rotating reps with the first-team offense in practice and preseason games. The Browns begin the 2026 regular season with two road games: Sept. 13 at the Jacksonville Jaguars and the following week at Tampa Bay. Cleveland's first home game is Sept. 27 against the Carolina Panthers. Despite reports the Browns were considering holding Sanders in the backup role until the home opener, Monken said Monday he's not entering into a "week-to-week thing" and expects Watson to excel. "Again, I think Shedeur has done a great job, come a long ways, and we're excited about his future. But this is not a week-to-week decision," he said. Cleveland covets stability at the position, and Watson was viewed as the potential answer when he was acquired from the Houston Texans prior to the 2022 season. As part of the trade, Watson signed a five-year, $230 million contract. But after starting his tenure with the team serving a suspension, he has been hindered by injuries and is just 9-10 as a starter in Cleveland. He hasn't played more than seven games in any of his four seasons with the Browns. Watson did not play last season while recovering from two surgeries to repair his Achilles. Watson tore his right Achilles tendon in October 2024 and a recurrence of the same injury during rehab prompted a second operation. Sanders, a fifth-round pick in 2025, was thrown into the lineup as a rookie. With Watson on injured reserve all season, the Browns began the season with Joe Flacco as the starter but traded him to the Cincinnati Bengals. Dillon Gabriel, a third-round rookie in 2025, was named the starter but Sanders took over in November. He had seven touchdown passes and 10 interceptions in eight games. Watson likely needs a strong start to the regular season to win back a fan base that appears to be running out of patience. Watson was showered with boos by home fans during Saturday's preseason game and said it was "personal." He played the second half against Buffalo and completed 5 of 12 passes for 36 yards and an interception "It's a little bit (more) personal than that. So I think it's a disrespectful thing," Watson said of being booed at home. "So yeah, I mean, I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. And yeah, just move on." Watson, who turns 31 the day after the Week 1 opener, used time with the media Monday to walk back some of his views on Browns fans. "... I think my emotions got the best of me," Watson said. "My comments wasn't intended to go at any of the fans around the city, because there's been a lot of great fans that have been supporting me." Monken, hired to replace Kevin Stefanski, is a first-time head coach after serving as the Baltimore Ravens' offensive coordinator for the last three seasons. He said Watson and the Browns can avoid being booed at home by playing better, but also offered his perspective on Watson's response. "I see the competitor in him. I see the everyday work he puts in, and he wants to be back," Monken said. "He wants to get back to where he was as best he can, and that's hard. And again, I think the moment just got him after the game, and it can get all of us." --Field Level Media

item.title: Monedas caen en medio de cautela de mercados a la espera de datos y Fed
item.description: Las principales monedas de América Latina iniciaron la semana con bajas, en medio de la cautela que ronda los mercados en una semana en la que se esperan datos y presentaciones de banqueros centrales que puedan dar orientación sobre el futuro de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Farías
item.content:encoded: Las principales monedas de América Latina iniciaron la semana con bajas, en medio de la cautela que ronda los mercados en una semana en la que se esperan datos y presentaciones de banqueros centrales que puedan dar orientación sobre el futuro de las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos. * La mirada, además, seguía puesta en la evolución de los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro, cuya alza de las últimas semanas ha generado preocupaciones sobre los costos del endeudamiento. * La cautela en las monedas era también generada por los acontecimientos sobre Oriente Medio, luego de que el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, anunció una ampliación de las sanciones secundarias que puede imponer a entidades y países que mantengan vínculos comerciales con Irán en todo el mundo. * El dólar avanzó a nivel global tras la ampliación de las sanciones contra Irán y la imposición de aranceles adicionales a los productos procedentes de Canadá. * La semana también estará marcada por los comentarios del presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, en el simposio de Jackson Hole, sobre la orientación de las tasas de interés. * El peso mayorista argentino se depreció un 0,66% al nivel mínimo histórico en 1.510 por cada dólar, su nivel mínimo histórico. El banco central (BCRA) argentino acumuló compras por 11 millones de dólares con el inicio de esta semana. * "El dólar mayorista quebró la barrera de los 1.500 (pesos) porque contenerlo a medida que pasa el tiempo exige esfuerzos mayores en términos de comprar menos reservas y subir tasas", dijo a Reuters Roberto Gerreto, analista de Adcap Grupo Financiero. * "Así, subas graduales del dólar van a permitir que no se atrase, facilitando la acumulación de reservas y no agregando estrés en las tasas. La clave será que no tenga ningún componente anunciado o sistemático, porque ello daría incentivos a dolarizar como ocurre cuando hay un 'crawling peg' formal", agregó. * Mientras, el índice S&P Merval (.MERV) de la Bolsa de Buenos Aires trepó un 2,81%, apoyada por el avance de acciones del rubro financiero. El Merval cayó un 1,2% la semana previa. * El peso mexicano bajaba hacia el cierre un 0,33%, a 16,9516 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) , integrado por las 35 acciones más líquidas del mercado, subió un ligero 0,06%, a 65.770,85 * "La moneda local enfrenta presiones por el fortalecimiento del dólar, el menor apetito por activos de mayor riesgo y las tensiones comerciales en Norteamérica, ante la cuarta revisión bilateral entre México y Estados Unidos, prevista para septiembre", dijo la correduría Monex. * La inflación general de México avanzó en la primera quincena de agosto, aunque menos de lo previsto, mientras que el índice subyacente se desaceleró de forma inesperada. * El real brasileño cedió un 0,23% a 5,1534 unidades por dólar, al tiempo que el referencial bursátil Bovespa (.BVSP) ganó un 0,6% a 172.055 puntos. * El peso colombiano terminó con baja de un 0,67% a 3.057 unidades por dólar, alejándose de máximos de casi ocho años; mientras que en la bolsa el índice accionario MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) se valorizó un 2,09% a 2.510,68 puntos. * El peso chileno , subió un 0,25%, en 912,50/912,80 unidades por dólar. En tanto, El índice principal de la Bolsa de Comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) , escaló un 1,76%, a 11.537,97 puntos. * La moneda peruana, el sol , finalizó la jornada con una leve depreciación del 0,06% a 3,3460/3,3470 unidades por dólar. En tanto que, la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) revirtió leves alzas y perdió un 0,18% a 1573,49 puntos.

item.title: Rendimiento de bonos EEUU cae mientras el Tesoro evalúa un cambio en su política de recompra
item.description: El rendimiento de los bonos de Estados Unidos caía el lunes, tras conocerse que el Departamento del Tesoro podría recurrir a su cuenta en efectivo para financiar un aumento de las recompras de deuda, mientras que los precios del petróleo retrocedieron.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: El rendimiento de los bonos de Estados Unidos caía el lunes, tras conocerse que el Departamento del Tesoro podría recurrir a su cuenta en efectivo para financiar un aumento de las recompras de deuda, mientras que los precios del petróleo retrocedieron. * La CNBC dio a conocer la noticia menos de una semana después de que el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, anunciara que el Gobierno duplicará, como mínimo, sus recompras de deuda a largo plazo, una medida inesperada que avivó la especulación sobre un enfoque más intervencionista para frenar el aumento de los rendimientos. * Esta medida supondría un cambio de rumbo, ya que las recompras están pensadas para ser neutras en términos de efectivo y se han financiado mediante emisiones, según explicó Molly Brooks, de TD Securities. * Los operadores siguen sopesando las implicaciones, sobre todo porque la decisión se produjo al margen del calendario habitual de refinanciación del Tesoro. A algunos les preocupa que la medida sea contraproducente y socave la confianza en el enfoque "regular y predecible" de la agencia respecto a la emisión de deuda. * "Si seguimos viendo este tipo de titulares que indican que podrían estar acelerando un poco las cosas, esa naturaleza regular y predecible podría, de hecho, aumentar la prima de plazo de los bonos del Tesoro a largo plazo", señaló Brooks. * Bessent afirmó el lunes que Estados Unidos continuaría con su programa habitual de subastas de bonos del Tesoro. * Esta situación complica aún más las perspectivas sobre las tasas de interés, ya que varias autoridades monetarias de la Reserva Federal han abogado por alzas en medio de una inflación persistentemente elevada. * Los operadores de futuros sobre los fondos federales están valorando en un 44% la probabilidad de un alza de tasas en la reunión de política monetaria del banco central de septiembre, cifra que se eleva al 78% para diciembre. * El rendimiento de los bonos a dos años , que suele evolucionar en línea con las expectativas de tasas, cotizaba estable en el 4,234%, y el de las notas referenciales a 10 años perdía 3,99 puntos básicos, al 4,698%. * La curva de rendimiento entre la deuda a dos y 10 años se aplanaba a 46 puntos básicos.

item.title: Peso argentino toca nivel mínimo histórico
item.description: El peso argentino en el mercado interbancario anotó el lunes su nivel mínimo histórico, con aval del Gobierno, tras romper la barrera psicológica de las 1.500 unidades por dólar para la venta.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso argentino en el mercado interbancario anotó el lunes su nivel mínimo histórico, con aval del Gobierno, tras romper la barrera psicológica de las 1.500 unidades por dólar para la venta. Los analistas coinciden en que es saludable la tendencia ya que hay un consenso generalizado de cierto atraso cambiario, en un país donde el dólar se usa como ahorro ante el resguardo inflacionario. Por su parte, las plazas de acciones y bonos del país sudamericano registraron mejoras dispares luego de finalizar en baja la semana previa ante la clara postura de prudencia por parte de los inversores. En el segmento mayorista , el peso nacional se depreció un 0,66% al nivel mínimo histórico en 1.510 por cada dólar, luego de cerrar la semana anterior en 1.500 unidades. "El dólar mayorista quebró la barrera de los 1.500 (pesos) porque contenerlo a medida que pasa el tiempo exige esfuerzos mayores en términos de comprar menos reservas y subir tasas", dijo a Reuters Roberto Geretto, analista de Adcap Grupo Financiero. "Así, subas graduales del dólar van a permitir que no se atrase, facilitando la acumulación de reservas y no agregando estrés en las tasas. La clave será que no tenga ningún componente anunciado o sistemático, porque ello daría incentivos a dolarizar como ocurre cuando hay un 'crawling peg' formal", agregó. El banco central (BCRA) argentino acumuló compras por 11 millones de dólares con el inicio de esta semana. Hasta la semana anterior, en "agosto las compras (del BCRA) acumulan 466 millones de dólares, un promedio de 33 millones de dólares diarios que profundiza la desaceleración frente a julio (103 millones diarios) y queda por debajo de junio (68 millones de dólares) y mayo (137 millones de dólares)", explicó el agente de compensación y liquidación Cohen. El índice S&P Merval (.MERV) de la Bolsa de Buenos Aires mejoró un firme 2,81% al cierre, apoyado por el avance de acciones del rubro financiero, contra una caída del 1,2% la semana previa. "Pese al freno del deterioro reciente, el mercado mantiene la cautela ante la duda de si este movimiento constituye una mejora de fondo o un mero rebote técnico", expresó la consultora Wise Capital. En tanto, los bonos soberanos en el segmento extrabursátil mejoraron apenas un 0,1% promedio, tras finalizar con un retroceso de 1,8% la semana pasada. El riesgo país, elaborado por el banco JP. Morgan, retrocedía algunos escalones hasta los 503 puntos básicos (2000 GMT). El llamado Índice de Confianza en el Gobierno (ICG) de la Universidad Torcuato Di Tella subió 2,4 puntos porcentuales a 41,2% en agosto, marcando la mayor mejora mensual desde noviembre. "La confianza en el Gobierno (del libertario Javier Milei) se mantiene elevada en relación a otras presidencias de este siglo", dijo el agente de liquidación y compensación Facimex. "La confianza en el Gobierno es clave por su correlación con los resultados electorales para el oficialismo", acotó.

item.title: S&P 500 y Nasdaq caen presionados por acciones tecnológicas; inversores analizan medidas sobre Irán
item.description: Los índices S&P 500 y Nasdaq descendieron el lunes, lastrados por las acciones tecnológicas, mientras los inversores sopesaban la nueva presión económica estadounidense contra Irán, a la espera esta semana de los resultados del gigante de la IA Nvidia y de un informe clave sobre la inflación.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Azhar, Purvi Agarwal, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: Los índices S&P 500 y Nasdaq descendieron el lunes, lastrados por las acciones tecnológicas, mientras los inversores sopesaban la nueva presión económica estadounidense contra Irán, a la espera esta semana de los resultados del gigante de la IA Nvidia y de un informe clave sobre la inflación. * El Gobierno de Donald Trump anunció el lunes una posible ampliación de las sanciones a los países que mantienen relaciones comerciales con Irán, en lo que denominó un "Día D económico", pero no llegó a imponer sanciones. * Las acciones de semiconductores cayeron, arrastrando al índice de semiconductores de Filadelfia (.SOX) . Nvidia (NVDA.O) bajó, al igual que Micron Technology (MU.O) y Broadcom (AVGO.O) , presionando al índice de tecnología de la información del S&P 500 (.SPLRCT) . * El sentimiento hacia las empresas tecnológicas también se vio afectado por la creciente oposición política a los centros de datos de IA. * El gobernador de Texas, Greg Abbott, lanzó una de las advertencias más contundentes hasta la fecha por parte de un republicano a la industria de la IA, afirmando que las firmas de centros de datos "cavaron su propia tumba" y merecen el rechazo que enfrentan tras no lograr el apoyo de la comunidad, informó Axios el domingo. * Sin embargo, el índice financiero (.SPSY) subió, con JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) y Visa (V.N) al alza. También contribuyeron a mantener a flote al índice Dow Jones. * Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) perdió 21,37 puntos, o un 0,28%, a 7.653,00 unidades. El Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) bajó 200,80 puntos, o un 0,77%, a 25.979,66 unidades; y el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) subió 141,67 puntos, o un 0,27%, a 53.418,68 unidades. * Se espera que los resultados trimestrales del gigante de la IA, Nvidia, sean otro catalizador clave para los mercados. Cualquier señal de desaceleración del crecimiento podría reavivar la preocupación por las elevadas valoraciones. * Los mercados también estarán atentos al informe de Gastos de Consumo Personal, el indicador de inflación preferido de la Fed, que se publicará el miércoles.

item.title: As US border reopens to Mexican cattle, concerns persist over screwworm spread
item.description: Mexico is bolstering its screwworm containment campaign in northern border states where recent cases have been detected, heightening scrutiny of livestock exports as cross-border trade resumed on Monday under a phased U.S. reopening.
item.dc:creator: Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: Mexico is bolstering its screwworm containment campaign in northern border states where recent cases have been detected, heightening scrutiny of livestock exports as cross-border trade resumed on Monday under a phased U.S. reopening. The reopening marks the first easing of a U.S. ban imposed more than a year ago to keep out the flesh-eating pest, as imports [USN:FWN43Q0OT TEXT:"resumed"] initially through Arizona . The plan has drawn criticism from some U.S. cattle groups and state officials who argue that resuming imports could increase screwworm risks even as the parasite continues to spread in northern Mexico and has already been detected in Texas and New Mexico. Mexican Agriculture Minister Columba Lopez said authorities would reinforce the dispersal of sterile flies in Sonora and Chihuahua, a key eradication strategy aimed at preventing the parasite from reproducing. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins told reporters on Monday that the USDA feels it has "taken every step to protect the American (cattle) herd and the American consumer, and so now we can slowly begin to reopen the ports." The USDA plans to open two more New Mexico ports, one in 30 days and another in 60 days, Rollins said. "We don't plan to open any Texas ports anytime soon just because that is where the real activity is," Rollins said. The USDA has identified 46 cases of screwworm in New Mexico and Texas, with two currently active, according to the agency's website. NEW CASES IN MEXICO A USDA website on Monday said it reopened the Douglas, Arizona, port to cattle imports from Mexico "guided by overlapping safeguards and a science-based import protocol" agreed upon by the two countries. The USDA will next evaluate the reopening of ports in Santa Teresa and Columbus, New Mexico, to cattle, bison, and horses. "The opening of ports may be paused if USDA identifies increased risk in Sonora or Chihuahua via post-opening audits or other observations/information," the site said. The reopening will begin with exports of 700 head of cattle per day during the first week, increasing to 900 per day in the second week and gradually rising to around 1,300 per day, according to Mexico’s National Confederation of Livestock Organizations (CNOG). If additional Chihuahua border crossings are reopened in the fourth quarter, Mexico could export up to 200,000 head of cattle in 2026, with an estimated value of about $420 million at U.S. market prices, CNOG said. Its base scenario for 2027 projects exports of 1.09 million head of cattle, valued at roughly $2.1 billion in the U.S. market. Chihuahua, one of Mexico's most important cattle-exporting states, has reported 183 confirmed screwworm cases since detecting its first case in July, while neighboring Sonora state has reported two confirmed cases after announcing its first detection last week. Sonora has activated emergency surveillance and containment protocols, while Chihuahua has intensified inspections, livestock movement controls and treatment campaigns to prevent further spread. The sterile insect technique works by releasing millions of sterilized screwworm flies that mate with wild females but produce no offspring, gradually driving down the pest population. Mexico recently opened a sterile-fly production plant in Chiapas, while the U.S. is building its own production facility in Texas, expected to be completed by the [USN:L6N4470WS TEXT:"spring of 2027"]. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum referred to the sterile-fly technique as a "modern" and "effective" way to fight screwworm. "That allows us to open the border," Sheinbaum said in her daily press conference.

item.title: A medida que la frontera de EEUU vuelve a abrirse al ganado mexicano, persiste preocupación por propagación del gusano barrenador
item.description: México está reforzando su campaña de contención de la mosca del gusano barrenador en los estados fronterizos del norte, donde se han detectado casos recientes, lo que ha intensificado los controles sobre las exportaciones de ganado tras la reanudación del comercio transfronterizo el lunes, en el marco de la reapertura gradual de Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas
item.content:encoded: México está reforzando su campaña de contención de la mosca del gusano barrenador en los estados fronterizos del norte, donde se han detectado casos recientes, lo que ha intensificado los controles sobre las exportaciones de ganado tras la reanudación del comercio transfronterizo el lunes, en el marco de la reapertura gradual de Estados Unidos. La secretaria de Agricultura de México, Columba López, afirmó que las autoridades reforzarían la liberación de moscas estériles en Sonora y Chihuahua, una estrategia clave de erradicación destinada a impedir que el parásito se reproduzca. "Vamos a mantener nosotros todo el sistema de trazabilidad desde la nacencia hasta que coloquemos el ganado del otro lado", dijo López en un enlace desde Sonora a la conferencia de prensa matutina de la presidente Claudia Sheinbaum. "Y la otra parte es reforzar la dispersión de moscas (vamos a) mantener muchísimos controles de seguridad", añadió. La reapertura gradual supone la primera flexibilización de[USN:L6N43Q1B0 TEXT:" la prohibición impuesta"] por Estados Unidos hace más de un año para impedir la entrada de esta plaga carnívora; está previsto que las importaciones se reanuden inicialmente a través de Arizona, antes de ampliarse a otros puertos de Nuevo México. El plan ha suscitado críticas por parte de algunas asociaciones ganaderas estadounidenses y de funcionarios estatales, que argumentan que la reanudación de las importaciones podría aumentar el riesgo de la mosca, incluso cuando el parásito sigue propagándose en el norte de México y ya se ha detectado en Texas y Nuevo México. El Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos (USDA por su sigla en inglés) había indicado anteriormente que la reapertura se llevaría a cabo por fases y que seguiría dependiendo del cumplimiento por parte de México de las medidas de control de la mosca del gusano. El lunes, la página en internet del USDA informó de que se había reabierto el puerto de Douglas, en Arizona, a las importaciones de ganado procedente de México, "guiándose por medidas de seguridad complementarias y un protocolo de importación con base científica" acordado por ambos países. El USDA evaluará la reapertura de los puertos de Santa Teresa y Columbus, en Nuevo México, al ganado vacuno, los bisontes y los caballos. "La apertura de los puertos podría suspenderse si el USDA detecta un aumento del riesgo en Sonora o Chihuahua a través de auditorías posteriores a la apertura u otras observaciones o información", indicó en el sitio. Chihuahua, uno de los estados mexicanos más importantes en la exportación de ganado, ha notificado 183 casos confirmados de gusano barrenador desde que detectó su primer caso en julio, mientras que el vecino estado Sonora ha notificado dos casos confirmados tras anunciar su primera detección la semana pasada. Sonora ha activado protocolos de vigilancia y contención de emergencia, mientras que Chihuahua ha intensificado las inspecciones, los controles de movimiento de ganado y las campañas de tratamiento para evitar una mayor propagación. La técnica de insectos estériles consiste en liberar millones de moscas esterilizadas que se aparean con hembras silvestres pero no producen descendencia, lo que reduce gradualmente la población de la plaga. México ha inaugurado recientemente una planta de producción de moscas estériles en Chiapas, mientras que Estados Unidos está construyendo su propia instalación de producción en Texas, cuya finalización está prevista para la primavera de 2027. La presidenta Sheinbaum se refirió a la técnica de la mosca estéril como una forma "moderna" y "eficaz" de combatir al gusano barrenador. "Eso nos permite que se abra la frontera", afirmó la mandataria en su rueda de prensa.

item.title: Trump amenaza arancel del 50% a todos los autos y camiones en disputa comercial con Canadá
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, declaró en una publicación en redes sociales el lunes que los aranceles a todos los autos y camiones, las autopartes y el acero se incrementarán al 50% a partir del 1 de enero de 2027, tras el fracaso de las negociaciones comerciales con Canadá.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, declaró en una publicación en redes sociales el lunes que los aranceles a todos los autos y camiones, las autopartes y el acero se incrementarán al 50% a partir del 1 de enero de 2027, tras el fracaso de las negociaciones comerciales con Canadá. El acuerdo comercial que se estaba negociando habría reducido la tasa arancelaria máxima sobre los autos y las furgonetas canadienses del 25% al 15%, y los gravámenes al aluminio y el acero del 50% al 25%. Sin embargo, se rompió por una serie de desacuerdos, como si la reducción arancelaria estadounidense se habría aplicado a los camiones de carga media o pesada. "Si se fabrica en Estados Unidos, los aranceles son CERO. ¡Canadá ya no recibirá el mismo trato que un estado!", escribió Trump. "En materia de comercio, y también en otros aspectos, se encuentran entre las peores naciones del mundo con las que tratar. Se creen con derecho a todo y, sin embargo, ¡NOSOTROS NO NECESITAMOS A CANADÁ, SON ELLOS LOS QUE NOS NECESITAN!", agregó. Trump quiere que Canadá se siente a la mesa y negocie de buena fe, declaró el lunes a periodistas el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent. En tanto, en una conferencia de prensa en Quebec, el primer ministro Mark Carney afirmó que era posible llegar a un "acuerdo mutuamente beneficioso" con Washington, pero únicamente si Estados Unidos respeta la soberanía de Canadá. "Cuando los estadounidenses se presenten primero a la mesa de negociaciones con la actitud correcta hacia nuestra industria y un verdadero espíritu de colaboración, por supuesto que nos sentaremos a negociar", señaló Carney. LAZOS DE COMERCIO, INTEGRACIÓN Canadá ha sido siempre uno de los dos principales socios comerciales de Estados Unidos. El año pasado, el comercio de bienes y servicios entre los países ascendió a 872.300 millones de dólares, lo que supone un descenso del 4,6%. Canadá exportó más de tres cuartas partes de sus productos a Estados Unidos e importó casi la mitad de los suyos de su vecino del sur. La producción de autos en Estados Unidos está muy integrada con la de Canadá y México, y los aranceles —dependiendo de los detalles— podrían tener repercusiones drásticas en la producción estadounidense. La Casa Blanca no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios en la que se pidieron más detalles sobre los aranceles con los que se había amenazado. Los representantes del Gobierno canadiense tampoco respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Canadá impondrá aranceles a algunos productos estadounidenses a partir del 8 de septiembre, en represalia por los gravámenes del 50% impuestos por Trump a productos canadienses por valor de 20.000 millones de dólares. "Estás en guerra cuando te atacan. Nos han atacado", declaró el sábado el primer ministro Mark Carney cuando se le preguntó si Canadá está inmerso en una guerra comercial. Muchos fabricantes de automóviles han anunciado o están barajando planes para reducir la producción en Canadá, y el enfrentamiento comercial ha provocado una reducción del 22% en las importaciones canadienses de vehículos estadounidenses. Los principales fabricantes de automóviles no se pronunciaron de inmediato sobre el anuncio de Trump. Sin embargo, algunos ejecutivos del sector, que hablaron con Reuters bajo condición de anonimato, se mostraron escépticos, señalando que Trump ya anunció antes aranceles elevados que nunca se materializaron y que cualquier gravamen de esa magnitud probablemente provocaría una represalia masiva por parte de Canadá. También señalaron que aún faltarán meses varios meses hasta enero tras las elecciones de mitad de mandato de noviembre y que la amenaza de Trump podría tener como objetivo reanudar las negociaciones.

item.title: Trump threatens 50% tariffs on all cars and trucks from Canada amid trade fight
item.description: President Donald Trump on Monday threatened to raise U.S. tariffs on all cars, trucks and automotive parts from Canada to 50% starting January 1, 2027, escalating a trade fight after negotiations collapsed last week.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson, Daphne Psaledakis
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump on Monday threatened to raise U.S. tariffs on all cars, trucks and automotive parts from Canada to 50% starting January 1, 2027, escalating a trade fight after [USN:T5N43900P TEXT:"negotiations collapsed last week"]. The trade deal on the table would have cut the top-line tariff rate on Canadian cars and light-duty trucks from 25% to 15% and the tariffs on aluminum and steel from 50% to 25%, but the deal fell apart on Friday over a number of points of contention, including whether the U.S. tariff relief would have applied to medium- or heavy-duty trucks. The escalation threatens to disrupt one of the world's most integrated auto supply chains. U.S. auto production is heavily reliant on Canadian-made parts and vehicles, and higher tariffs could raise costs for American automakers and consumers while deepening a trade standoff that has already weighed on auto stocks. "Build in the U.S. and there are ZERO TARIFFS. Canada will be treated like a State no longer!" Trump wrote in a social media post. "On Trade, and in other ways, also, they are among the worst Nations in the World to deal with. They feel entitled, and yet, WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!" Trump said. Trump wants Canada to come to the table and negotiate in good faith, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters on Monday. At a press conference in Quebec on Monday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said a "mutually beneficial deal" with the U.S. was possible, but only if Americans respect Canada's sovereignty. "When the Americans go to the negotiating table first with the right attitude toward our industry and a true partnership, of course we'll come to the negotiating table," Carney said at a briefing announcing an investment in six new Canadian icebreaker ships. AUTO STOCKS DECLINE ON TRUMP WARNING Auto stocks fell on the news. Shares of Ford (F.N) and Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , were down 3.6% and 4.2%, respectively, while shares of General Motors (GM.N) were down 1.6% on Monday afternoon. Toyota (7203.T) , stock was down 1.5% in New York trading and Honda (7267.T) , shares were down 2.1%. Canada has consistently been one of the top two U.S. trading partners and last year, U.S. goods and services trade with Canada totaled $872.3 billion, down 4.6%. Canada exported about three-quarters of its goods to the U.S. and imported almost half of its goods from the U.S., the U.S. Trade Representative's Office said. Flavio Volpe, president of Canada's Automotive Parts Manufacturers' Association, said: "A threatened U.S. tariff on Canadian auto parts will be paid by (the) US auto assembly. Without those specific parts, auto assembly throughout the U.S. would halt." The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment seeking more details on the threatened tariffs. CANADA ANNOUNCES RETALIATORY TARIFFS [USN:L1N44J034 TEXT:"Canada will impose tariffs"] on some U.S. goods starting September 8 in retaliation for 50% levies ordered by Trump on $20 billion in Canadian products. "You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked," Carney said on Saturday when asked whether Canada was engaged in a trade war. Three in four Canadians approved of Carney’s decision to walk away from trade negotiations with the United States late on Friday night, according to an opinion poll by the Angus Reid Institute on Sunday. Many automakers have announced or are considering plans to scale back Canadian auto production and the trade standoff has led to a 22% reduction in Canadian imports of U.S. vehicles, according to the White House. Major automakers did not immediately comment on Trump's announcement. INDUSTRY SKEPTICISM OVER TARIFF Auto executives, speaking to Reuters on condition of anonymity, raised skepticism about Trump's threat, noting that he has previously announced tariffs that were later scaled back or delayed. They also noted that January was months after the upcoming U.S. midterm elections in November, and that Trump's threat could be aimed at restarting talks. In January of this year, Trump said the U.S. would decertify Bombardier Global Express business jets and threatened 50% import tariffs on all aircraft made in Canada until the country's regulator certified a number of planes produced by U.S. rival Gulfstream. Neither occurred, but [USN:L1N3ZK0S8 TEXT:"the following month Canada certified"] several Gulfstream planes.

item.title: Strategy earmarks $1.6 billion cash pool for treasury operations, buybacks
item.description: Michael Saylor's Strategy set aside about $1.6 billion in cash to fund future treasury operations, including potential bitcoin purchases and share buybacks, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Saylor's Strategy (MSTR.O) set aside about $1.6 billion in cash to fund future treasury operations, including potential bitcoin purchases and share buybacks, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing on Monday. The world's largest corporate buyer of bitcoin dubbed the liquidity pool "USD Cash," which will be different from a reserve it set up earlier to fund dividends on its preferred stock and interest on its outstanding debt. The new cash pool will have more flexible uses and could be used for bitcoin purchases, share buybacks and other corporate events. It could also give Strategy more flexibility to navigate bitcoin market downturns, allowing it to maintain cash on hand, while continuing to pursue its bitcoin-buying strategy. The move comes after a robust week for bitcoin, which gained a little over 13% in the last five sessions after U.S. President Donald Trump urged Congress to pass legislation establishing clear rules for digital assets. Bitcoin breached the $70,000 mark last week, for the first time since June. Risk assets, like cryptocurrencies, have also benefited after the U.S. Treasury Department's move to double buyback sizes for long-duration debt reined in yields. Higher yields are typically a negative for such assets because they increase the returns on safer investments. Still, bitcoin remains far from the peaks it hit after a staggering run last year.

item.title: Washington Post ordered to reinstate columnist Karen Attiah
item.description: A private arbitrator ordered the newspaper to reinstate Attiah with back pay after she was fired over social media posts about Charlie Kirk's assassination.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A private arbitrator has ordered The Washington Post to reinstate opinion columnist Karen Attiah with back pay, after the newspaper fired her in September over social media posts about conservative activist [USN:L2N3UX0YE TEXT:"Charlie Kirk's assassination"]. The ruling, made public by the Democracy Defenders Fund on Monday, comes as the Post's opinion section faces scrutiny following a push by owner Jeff Bezos to focus on [USN:L2N3PH0XF TEXT:"personal liberties and free markets"]. Here are some more details: Private arbitrator Sarah Miller Espinosa found the newspaper "did not have good and sufficient cause" to terminate Attiah and had "violated" its labor agreement. "The Washington Post failed to establish the grievant engaged in gross misconduct," she wrote. "This decision confirms what we've said from the start: I was doing my job as an opinion journalist, and doing that job is not misconduct," said Attiah. A Washington Post spokesperson said the newspaper respects the arbitration process and declined to comment further. The dispute began after Attiah's posts on social media platform Bluesky following Kirk's September 2025 assassination, including one in which she noted Kirk's past comments on Black women. The Post had said in its termination letter that Attiah's posts violated its social media policy, which requires employees' online activity to be respectful and not undermine the integrity of the newspaper's journalism. In February, The Washington Post [USN:L6N3Z015A TEXT:"began layoffs"] impacting a third of its employees, across its international, editing, metro and sports desks amid mounting financial losses. The New York Times first reported the arbitration decision earlier in the day.

item.title: EUA ameaçam países que negociam com o Irã, mas ainda não aplicam penalidades
item.description: O governo do presidente Donald Trump anunciou nesta segunda-feira uma possível ampliação das sanções contra países que mantêm relações comerciais com o Irã, como parte do que foi anunciado como um “Dia D econômico”, mas não chegou a impor as penalidades de fato.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Humeyra Pamuk
item.content:encoded: O governo do presidente Donald Trump anunciou nesta segunda-feira uma possível ampliação das sanções contra países que mantêm relações comerciais com o Irã, como parte do que foi anunciado como um “Dia D econômico”, mas não chegou a impor as penalidades de fato. À medida que a guerra com o Irã se aproxima da marca de seis meses, o secretário do Tesouro, Scott Bessent, afirmou que os EUA estavam lançando uma “ofensiva econômica” contra as conexões financeiras do Irã em todo o mundo. Mas Bessent se recusou a dizer quais países específicos seriam alvo das medidas, ou quando essas penalidades entrariam em vigor. “Por que eu iria querer destruir o sistema financeiro global? Acreditamos que é importante estabelecer um ponto de equilíbrio e dar às pessoas um período de adaptação, mas elas devem saber que isso avançará muito rapidamente e que estamos falando sério”, disse ele em uma coletiva de imprensa. Bessent antecipou um “grande anúncio” sobre sanções contra uma instituição financeira até o final da semana. A China tem sido, há vários anos, a maior compradora de petróleo iraniano, e Washington tem intensificado seus esforços para coibir as compras chinesas, mas até o momento não chegou a aplicar sanções contra os maiores bancos chineses. Com o encontro marcado entre Trump e o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, em Washington no final de setembro, novas sanções contra bancos chineses poderiam prejudicar as perspectivas de prorrogação de um acordo firmado em novembro passado para manter o fluxo de terras raras chinesas e limitar as tarifas dos EUA. A guerra de Trump contra o Irã, que elevou os preços da energia em todo o mundo, está prestes a completar seis meses. Embora os combates intensos tenham diminuído, os esforços diplomáticos para pôr fim à guerra estão estagnados e o transporte de petróleo e matérias-primas pelo Estreito de Ormuz continua bloqueado, mantendo os preços da energia elevados. Bessent também anunciou sanções contra quase 60 entidades, indivíduos e embarcações, e afirmou que o Tesouro estava visando cinco setores que o Irã utilizava para sustentar sua economia: ativos digitais, ouro, tecnologia, aviação e transporte marítimo. A guerra de Trump contra o Irã, que elevou os preços da energia em todo o mundo, está prestes a completar seis meses. Embora os combates intensos tenham diminuído, os esforços diplomáticos para pôr fim à guerra estão paralisados e o transporte de petróleo e matérias-primas pelo Estreito de Ormuz continua bloqueado, mantendo os preços da energia elevados. A popularidade de Trump caiu para seu nível mais baixo, com apenas 33% dos norte-americanos, segundo a última pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos, aprovando seu desempenho. Ele afirma que os custos econômicos são necessários para garantir que o Irã não possua uma arma nuclear. DÉCADAS DE SANÇÕES Os EUA mantêm sanções contra o Irã há décadas, a maioria das quais visa restringir as receitas do país com o petróleo, o setor de aviação, as criptomoedas, a aquisição de componentes de armas e outros equipamentos militares, além de cortar o financiamento para empresas controladas pela Guarda Revolucionária Islâmica, uma força dominante na economia iraniana. As sanções impedem que entidades designadas tenham acesso ao sistema financeiro baseado no dólar, mas o Irã tem conseguido criar rapidamente novas empresas de fachada, outras entidades e registros de embarcações para contornar as sanções. Nos últimos meses, o Tesouro sancionou refinarias chinesas independentes, conhecidas como "teapots", por comprar petróleo iraniano e ampliou suas medidas contra a frota fantasma de petroleiros que transporta petróleo iraniano. O bloqueio dos EUA aos portos do Irã já reduziu as ofertas chinesas de compra de petróleo bruto iraniano, informou a Reuters na sexta-feira, o que pode diminuir o impacto das sanções secundárias sobre a China. Os Estados Unidos, a Organização das Nações Unidas e a União Europeia têm aplicado sanções, implementado embargos comerciais e congelado ativos desde o final da década de 1970 devido ao programa nuclear do Irã, às violações dos direitos humanos e ao apoio a grupos militantes. Dados do Departamento do Tesouro dos EUA mostram que foram impostas sanções relacionadas ao Irã a mais de 1.000 pessoas, embarcações e aeronaves desde que Trump iniciou seu segundo mandato em 2025. Medidas recentes têm como alvo a frota fantasma de petróleo do Irã; seguradoras de transporte marítimo; entidades e pessoas que facilitam a aquisição de armas pelo Irã; e plataformas de câmbio digital, congelando cerca de US$500 bilhões em criptomoedas ligadas ao Irã.

item.title: US threatens countries doing business with Iran, but holds off on penalties for now
item.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday announced a possible expansion of sanctions on countries doing business with Iran as part of what it billed as an "economic D-Day," but stopped short of actually imposing penalties.
item.dc:creator: David Lawder, Humeyra Pamuk
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's administration on Monday announced a possible expansion of sanctions on countries doing business with Iran as part of what it billed as an "economic D-Day," but stopped short of actually imposing penalties. As the war with Iran nears its six-month mark, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. was launching an "economic onslaught" against Iran's financial connections around the globe. But he declined to say what specific countries would be targeted, or when those penalties would take effect. The Treasury Department announced new sanctions on 60 individuals, entities and vessels but that list did not include any of the Chinese financial institutions suspected of facilitating Iran's oil trade. "Why would I want to blow up the global financial system? We believe that it is important to level set and give people a cure period, but they should know that that will move very quickly and that we are serious," Bessent told a press conference. China has for several years been the biggest buyer of Iranian oil, and Washington has intensified its efforts to clamp down on Chinese purchases, but has so far stopped short of targeting larger Chinese banks with sanctions. With Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping scheduled to meet in Washington in late September, new sanctions on Chinese banks could sour prospects for extending a deal struck last November to keep Chinese rare earths flowing and cap U.S. tariffs. Tuesday's action targeted businesses in China, the UAE, Singapore and several other countries, including a cooking-oil refinery in France. Bessent said the U.S. was targeting five sectors Iran was using to prop up its economy: digital assets, gold, technology, aviation and shipping. He previewed a "major announcement" of sanctions on a financial institution by the end of the week but a Treasury spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for more information. Trump's war with Iran, which has pushed energy prices higher worldwide, is about to hit its six-month mark. While heavy fighting has subsided, diplomatic efforts to end the war have stalled and oil and raw material shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked, keeping energy prices elevated. Trump's approval rating has fallen to a low point, with just 33% of Americans in the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll approving of his performance. He says the economic costs are necessary to ensure Iran does not have a nuclear weapon. DECADES OF SANCTIONS The U.S. has maintained sanctions against Iran for decades, most of which have been aimed at curtailing the country's oil revenues, aviation sector, cryptocurrency, procurement of weapons components and other military hardware, and cutting off funding for business enterprises controlled by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, a dominant force in the Iranian economy. The sanctions bar designated entities from the dollar-based financial system, but Iran has been successful in quickly standing up new front companies, other entities and vessel registrations to evade the sanctions. The Treasury Department has also recently sanctioned independent Chinese "teapot" refineries for buying Iranian oil, and expanded sanctions on the "shadow fleet" of tankers transporting Iranian oil. Tehran has managed to weather decades of U.S. sanctions but the naval blockade that the U.S. imposed has inflicted severe economic damage on the country. That already curbed Chinese offers to purchase Iranian crude, [USN:L1N44I07T TEXT:"Reuters reported on Friday"], which may lessen the impact of secondary sanctions on China. Earlier this month, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States could maintain the naval blockade indefinitely, which could keep oil prices elevated, potentially stirring U.S. voter anger ahead of congressional elections in November. Treasury Department data shows the U.S. has imposed Iran-related sanctions on more than 1,000 people, vessels and aircraft since Trump began his second term in 2025. Recent measures have targeted Iran's shadow oil fleet, shipping insurers, weapons-procurement network, and digital exchanges, freezing an estimated $500 billion in Iran-linked cryptocurrency. Bessent singled out Iran's Bank Melli, which continues to operate branches in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. "Every branch of Bank Melli must be shuttered and dark," he said.

item.title: Crudo cae más de 2 dólares pese a nuevas sanciones de EEUU contra Irán
item.description: Los precios del petróleo cayeron más de 2 dólares por barril el lunes ya que los inversores recogieron beneficios tras las recientes alzas y no prestaron atención a las nuevas sanciones de Estados Unidos contra Irán.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo cayeron más de 2 dólares por barril el lunes ya que los inversores recogieron beneficios tras las recientes alzas y no prestaron atención a las nuevas sanciones de Estados Unidos contra Irán. * Los futuros del crudo Brent cerraron con caída de 2,22 dólares, o un 2,35%, hasta los 92,17 dólares, mientras que el crudo estadounidense West Texas Intermediate cayó 2,05 dólares por barril, un 2,35% menos, hasta situarse en 85,01 dólares. * El secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, anunció el lunes una ampliación de las sanciones secundarias que puede imponer a entidades y países que mantengan vínculos comerciales con Irán en todo el mundo, en un momento en que Washington intensifica significativamente la presión económica sobre Teherán. * Lo anterior se produjo tras las amenazas de Trump de "guerra económica y aislamiento a una escala sin precedentes" contra Teherán la semana pasada. * "No hay muchas novedades en las declaraciones de Bessent, más allá de lo que ya se había adelantado", afirmó Pavel Molchanov, analista de estrategia de inversión de Raymond James. Añadió que el mercado del petróleo, tras repuntar bastante la semana pasada, registró una toma de beneficios. * Ambos contratos registraron la semana pasada su segunda alza semanal consecutiva, con un aumento superior al 5%. * "La verdadera pregunta ahora es hasta qué punto está dispuesto Washington a aplicar con dureza sanciones secundarias contra los socios comerciales que aún le quedan a Irán", señaló Jorge León, jefe de análisis geopolítico de Rystad Energy. "A menos que China reduzca sustancialmente sus compras, el impacto adicional sobre los ingresos petroleros iraníes podría ser relativamente limitado", añadió. * Irán había condenado los planes de Estados Unidos de anunciar nuevas sanciones y el presidente Masoud Pezeshkian había abogado por una solución diplomática. El jefe del ejército de Pakistán estaba de visita en Teherán el lunes para mantener conversaciones de mediación, antes del anuncio. * Los envíos de petróleo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, una ruta por la que antes circulaba una quinta parte del suministro mundial, siguieron viéndose limitados. * Menos de 20 buques de mercancías transitaron por el estrecho de Ormuz el fin de semana, según datos de transporte marítimo publicados el lunes, ya que los bloqueos iraníes y estadounidenses restringen el tráfico a través de este punto estratégico para los envíos de energía.

item.title: nVent Electric to buy Maverick Power for $1.75 billion to expand data center offerings
item.description: nVent Electric said on Monday it would acquire data center equipment maker Maverick Power for $1.75 billion as it looks to expand its presence in a booming AI infrastructure market.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: nVent Electric (NVT.N) said on Monday it would acquire data center equipment maker Maverick Power for $1.75 billion as it looks to expand its presence in a booming AI infrastructure market. Electrical equipment and systems suppliers like nVent have benefited as companies ramp up investment to support the rapid expansion of AI computing capacity, with CEO Beth Wozniak saying the Maverick acquisition will add power distribution capabilities and strengthen its offerings to data center customers. The deal also includes a potential additional consideration of up to $550 million in cash if Maverick achieves certain performance targets in 2027 and 2028, nVent said. McKinney, Texas-based Maverick Power makes engineered power distribution and infrastructure solutions, including low- and medium-voltage switchgears and switchboards, and integrated modular solutions. nVent expects to fund the deal with a combination of cash on hand and new debt. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approval. Shares of London-based nVent were down 1.3% in premarket trading.

item.title: Dólar sube tras sanciones a Irán, dólar canadiense cae por tras anuncio de aranceles EEUU
item.description: El dólar subió el lunes, después de que el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump anunciara una ampliación de las sanciones contra Irán y la imposición de aranceles adicionales a los productos procedentes de Canadá.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
